reflection_text.5:
The discussion converges on the prefix–suffix model for a fixed strand orientation. On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand the two founders are
$P_{0}=00000$, $P_{1}=11111$.  With one obligatory single break per meiosis an $F_{1}$ gamete is monotone
$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, $|H_{1}|=6$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i)$ for $i\le k$ and $h_{b}(i)$ for $i>k$
with $a,b,k\in\{0,\dots ,5\}$ on the positive strand.  With $m=\min(a,k)$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$, 

so the only possible descent $1\to0$ can occur at the junction $k\to k+1$.
Hence a positive-strand word is $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$,
$b\ge0$, $c\ge0$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The monotone $c_{0}$ words
are $0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $t=0\ldots5$, $n+1=6$ of them.  For a descent at
position $i$ the prefix can be chosen in $i$ ways and the suffix in $5-i$
ways, $N_{1}(i)=i(5-i)$.  Thus

$N_{1}= \sum_{i=1}^{4}i(5-i)=4+6+6+4=20$

words have exactly one $1\to0$, e.g. $01011,00101,\dots$, and

$N=n+1+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}i(n-i)=6+20=26$

different positive-strand haplotypes can be present in an $F_{3}$ chromosome.
In closed form $N(n)=(n+1)(n^{2}-n+6)/6$, $N(5)=26$.  The six monotone
$F_{1}$ haplotypes are $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$ and the
$20$ genuinely new $F_{3}$ haplotypes are the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$
with $0\le a<k<b\le5$, i.e. all binary words of length five with at most
one $1\to0$ descent.

With $H=26$ distinct haplotypes the ordered diploid pool is $H^{2}=676$
and the unordered diploid genotypes are
$H(H+1)/2=26\times27/2=351$, the $6$ monotone haplotypes being the
ordinary $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ set.

Disagreements noted.  Colleagues 2,8 quote the textbook $t$-break count
$2\sum_{k\le t}\binom{4}{k}$ i.e. $11$ per phase, $22$ with the two
phases counted, which is the $\le2$ parental-origin-break count.  Colleague
4/9 obtain the $2^{\,3}=8$ $0\ldots1$ strings $0x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}1$ on the
strict $0\to1$ phase with mandatory interior cuts.  The $22$-haplotype
and $8$-haplotype numbers are the conventional phase-symmetric or
mandatory-interior-cut variants; the $26$ haplotype, $351$ genotype,
count is the orientation-fixed prefix-suffix count usually quoted for two
successive one-crossover meioses with the trivial $k=0,5$ ends admitted.
The $2^{5}-2=30$ maximal combinatorial realisation is reached only after a
third meiosis.  Unresolved is whether telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ should be
excluded for a strictly mandatory crossover; with $k,a,b\in\{1..4\}$ the
non-monotone core is the $20$ words above, the $26$ count being the
conventional inclusive one.
reflection_text.9:
The five SNPs are binary on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand, P0=00000, P1=11111.  One orientation-fixed one-crossover meiosis from P0/P1 gives the monotone F1 gamete set

H1 = {0^t 1^{5-t} : 0≤t≤5}, |H1|=6, 
the 0→1 thresholds 11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000.

An F2 individual is h_a/h_b with h_a,h_b∈H1.  An F2→F3 gamete on the
positive strand is the orientation-fixed prefix-suffix product

rec_k(h_a,h_b)[i]=h_a(i) i≤k , h_b(i) i>k , 0≤k≤5.

Writing h_a=0^a1^{5-a}, h_b=0^b1^{5-b} gives

rec_k = 0^{min(a,k)}1^{k-min(a,k)}0^{max(0,b-k)}1^{5-max(b,k)} .

If a≥k or b≤k the product is a threshold, i.e. rec_k∈H1.  The
non-trivial case is a<k<b where

rec_k(h_a,h_b)=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},        0≤a<k<b≤5,

a uniquely the length of the initial 0-run, k the end of the first
1-run and b the end of the second 0-run.  Distinct triples (a,k,b) with
a<k<b give distinct words.  Number of such triples is C(6,3)=20.
Adding the six thresholds gives

|H2| = 6 + C(6,3)=6+20=26

different positive-strand haplotypes that can be present in an
F3 gamete and hence in an F3 chromosome.  The 6 monotone words are the
F1 gametes, the 20 words 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} with a<k<b are the
genuinely new two-meiosis mosaics, e.g. 10111,10011,…,11110,01110, etc.

In diploid terms the 26 haplotypes can be paired arbitrarily, 26^2
ordered pairs, 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 genotypes.  The 26 count is the
concatenation-of-two-monotone-words count N(n)=(n+1)+n(n-1)(n+1)/6,
N(5)=26.

This is distinct from the classic “at most t breaks per lineage’’ count
∑_{k=0}^{t}C(4,k)=11 per parental phase, 22 total phases, which
follows if a haplotype is required to acquire at most t breaks in its
own ancestry.  The 11/22/8 figures quoted by several colleagues are that
text-book ≤2-break count, or its 0…1 phase-restricted version.  Under
the literal one crossover per gamete per generation with strand
asymmetry the F3 gamete is rec_k of two F1 thresholds, which permits up
to one 1→0 descent and hence the 26 haplotypes, 20 genuinely new on the
positive strand, the usual 2^5−2=30 maximal binary words being reached
only after a third meiosis.  Unresolved is whether the question wants
haplotype number 26 or unordered diploid number 351; the 22-haplotype,
11-per-phase conventional count is the competing interpretation.
reflection_text.1:
The five diallelic sites can be coded 0 = strain A allele, 1 = strain B allele on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand. With fixed orientation a single meiosis in a heterozygote $h_{a}/h_{b}$ produces on the positive strand
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]\,h_{b}[k+1:5]$, $0\le k\le5$.
The two inbred founders are $0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$.

F1. On the positive strand the monotone $0\to1$ gametes are
$S_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}$, $|S_{1}|=6$. With the strict
“exactly one crossover per gamete’’ convention the two telomeric
$k=0,5$ cases are the trivial parental products; the non-trivial F1
gametes are the four $k=1\ldots4$ mosaics
$01111,00111,00011,00001$.

F2→F3. An F3 chromosome is ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ with
$h_{a},h_{b}\in S_{1}$. Writing $h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$,
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with
$m=\min(a,k)$, $b\ge k$. Up to the $k=0,5$ trivial cases the
non-trivial words are
$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<k<b\le5$.
$a$ is the length of the initial $0$-run, $k$ the end of the first
$1$-run and $b$ the end of the second $0$-run; the triple is unique.

With the conventional $k=0,5$ ends kept as formal recombinants the
positive-strand set is
$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ with $n=5$,
$|H_{2}|=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$.
The six monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{1}$ thresholds and
the $20=\binom{6}{3}$ words $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with
$0\le a<k<b\le5$ are the genuinely new two-meiosis mosaics, e.g.
$10111,10011,\dots,01110,00110,00010$.
In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered $F_{3}$ genotypes.

Strict one-crossover interpretation. If $k=0,5$ are excluded,
$S_{1}^{\rm nt}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}$ has 4 elements. Then
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ with $1\le k\le4$ is
$0^{p}1^{k-p}0^{q}1^{5-k-q}$ with $1\le p\le k$, $0\le q\le4-k$.
The distinct positive-strand words are exactly the $0\,xxx\,1$ words,
$2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ haplotypes:
$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$,
i.e. $k(5-k)$ words per $k$ with total $20$ counted with multiplicity,
$8$ distinct. This is $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes.
Counting the reciprocal $1\to0$ phase doubles the conventional
counts to $2\sum_{k\le2}\binom{4}{k}=22$ haplotypes, $11$ per fixed
phase, and the maximal combinatorial set with both phases is
$2\sum_{k\le3}\binom{4}{k}=30=2^{5}-2$.

The 26-haplotype, 351-genotype figure is the one usually quoted for
two successive orientation-fixed single-crossover meioses with the
trivial $k=0,5$ ends included; the 8-haplotype, 36-genotype figure is
the strict exactly-one-crossover per gamete realization. The
disagreement in the room is essentially the inclusion/exclusion of the
$k=0,5$ parental products and whether the count is haploid vs
diploid and per phase vs both phases.
reflection_text.2:
The founders can be put on the arbitrarily chosen + strand as

P0 = 0^5 , P1 = 1^5 .

With the orientation fixed a F1 meiosis is the prefix–suffix operation

rec_k(h_a,h_b)= h_a[1:k] h_b[k+1:5] , 0≤k≤5 ,

on the two homologues.  The monotone F1 gamete pool is

S1 = { h_t =0^t1^{5-t} : 0≤t≤5 } , |S1|=6,

the 4 interior ones 0^1 1^4…0^4 1^1 being the genuinely one-crossover
gametes.  An F2→F3 gamete is rec_k(h_a,h_b) with h_a,h_b∈S1.  With
a = min(a,k) the word is

rec_k(h_a,h_b)=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} , m =min(a,k) ,

i.e. a concatenation of a monotone prefix and a monotone suffix.  On the
+ strand the only descent 1→0 that can be created is the descent at the
junction k→k+1.

* With the formal k=0,5 ends kept the three numbers a<k<b give the
non-monotone words

h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a<k<b≤5,

which are in 1-1 correspondence with triples a<k<b.  There are
C(6,3)=20 of them.  Together with the 6 monotone words

0^5,0^4 1,0^3 1^2,0^2 1^3,0^1 1^4,1^5

the + strand gamete pool that can be made by two successive
orientation-fixed one-crossover meioses is

|H2| = (n+1)+C(n+1,3)=6+20=26 ,  n=5,

26 different + strand haplotypes, 20 genuinely new in F3.  Up to order
that is 26·27/2=351 unordered diploid F3 autosomes, 26² ordered pairs.
This is the 6+ n(n-1)(n+1)/6 = 26 count quoted by Colleagues 1,3,5,6.

If the “exactly one interior crossover per gamete’’ is enforced strictly,
k=0,5 and a=0,5 are not allowed.  Then S1_strict = {0^t1^{5-t}:1≤t≤4}
and k∈{1,2,3,4}.  The rec_k(h_a,h_b) set collapses to the
0…1 words with the first and last marker fixed by the founders.
The three interior markers are free, i.e.

{0 x1 x2 x3 1 : xi∈{0,1}} ,

2^{3}=8 distinct + strand haplotypes

01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101,

the four monotone F1 haplotypes persisting because a crossover can fall
in a region of identity between two different F1 haplotypes.  That is the
8-haplotype, 8·9/2=36 unordered diploid genotype bound quoted by
Colleagues 9 and 4, and the 2^{n-2} bound.  Formally including the
telomeric k=0,5 ends recovers the 26-haplotype set above.

The split in the room is therefore:

* formal / textbook count with k=0,5 allowed: 26 + strand haplotypes,
  351 unordered diploid F3 genotypes;
* strict interior-one-crossover count: 8 + strand haplotypes,
  36 unordered diploid F3 genotypes, i.e. 4 monotone + 4 with a single
  1→0 descent.

The 22 / 11 / 30 figures are the conventional ≤2-break counts
2∑_{k≤2}C(4,k)=22 haplotypes counting the two complementary phases,
11 per phase, which relaxes the monotone-prefix-suffix structure to an
ordinary ≤2-break count.  The unresolved modelling choice is whether
k=0,5 is to be kept as a formal recombination and whether the question
asks for haplotype diversity or for diploid genotype diversity.
reflection_text.3:
The discussion centres on the set of positive-strand haplotypes that can be made by two successive single-crossover meioses starting from 00000 / 11111 with the recombination product fixed to prefix of homolog A followed by suffix of homolog B.

* P0 = 00000 , P1 = 11111. With the orientation fixed a meiosis of a A/B heterozygote gives the monotone family
H1 = {0^{k}1^{5-k} : 0≤k≤5}. |H1|=6, 4 of them are internal.
The F1 chromosome pool is H1.

* An F2 → F3 gamete is rec_k(h_a , h_b) with h_a =0^{a}1^{5-a}, h_b=0^{b}1^{5-b} in H1 and 0≤k≤5. On the positive strand
rec_k = 0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} , m = min(a,k). 
Hence every F3 haplotype is of the form 0^{p}1^{q}0^{r}1^{s} with p+q+r+s=5, i.e. at most one 1→0 descent.

With the usual textbook inclusive convention k=0,5 allowed,
# monotone = n+1 =6,
# with exactly one descent at position i = i·(n-i), i=1..4,
N1 = Σ i(n-i)=4+6+6+4=20.
N =6+20=26 distinct positive-strand haplotypes.
The 6 monotone = 0^{t}1^{5-t}, the 20 new are the 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} with 0≤a<k<b≤5.  The triple (a,k,b) is a unique decoder. This is the (n+1)+C(n+1,3) =6+20=26 count quoted by Colleagues 1,3,5,6,10.  In diploid terms H=26 gives 26^2=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered genotypes.

Disagreement in the room:
* Strict ‘exactly one internal crossover per gamete’ removes the k=0,5 trivial cases. Then H1 internal = {0^{k}1^{5-k},1≤k≤4}, |H1|=4. With a,b,k′∈{1..4} the reachable set is monotone p=1..4 plus the non-monotone 0^{p}1^{k′-p}0^{b-k′}1^{5-b} with b>k′. That gives Σk′(4−k′)=10 non-monotone plus 4 monotone =14 positive-strand haplotypes, 8 of them starting 0 ending 1. Colleagues 4,8,9 are moving toward this stricter counting, e.g. the 2^{n-2}=8 strings 0xxxx1.

* The classic ‘at most t breaks from the founders’ count is Σ_{k=0}^{t}C(4,k). On a fixed 0→1 phase this is 1+4+6=11 haplotypes, 22 counting the two phases, the 2ΣC(4,k) figures quoted by Colleagues 2,8. That is the number of strings with ≤2 parental breakpoints, not the number obtainable as a concatenation of two monotone F1 haplotypes with fixed orientation.

Unresolved: whether ‘exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’ is to be read as strictly internal k=1..4 in every meiosis, in which case the inclusive 26 count overestimates, and whether the question asks for haploid haplotypes or diploid autosome genotypes. The 26-haplotype, 351-genotype inclusive result is the consensus in the current round.

different words with exactly one 1→0 descent, i.e. the form

reflection_text.6:
The two founder chromosomes can be written on the arbitrarily
chosen strand as $0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$.  Up to the sign convention a single
orientation fixed meiosis produces on the positive strand the monotone
mosaics

$$H_{1}=\{0^{a}1^{5-a}\;,\;0\le a\le5\},\qquad |H_{1}|=6 ,$$

the six $F_{1}$ gametes $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Let $h_{a}(i)=0\;i\le a,\;1\;i>a$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\;h_{b}(i),\;i>k$,

$0\le k\le5$.  On the positive strand both the prefix and the suffix are
$0\!\to\!1$ monotone, so a word is reachable iff it can be split at some
$k$ into a monotone prefix and a monotone suffix.  With
$a<k<b$

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad 0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$ descent.
For a fixed descent position $i$, $1\le i\le4$, the prefix can be chosen
in $i$ ways $0^{p}1^{i-p}$, $0\le p<i$, and the suffix in $5-i$ ways
$0^{q}1^{5-i-q}$, $1\le q\le5-i$.  Hence

$$N_{1}(i)=i(5-i),\qquad 
N_{1}=\sum_{i=1}^{4}i(5-i)=4+6+6+4=20 $$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  With the $n+1=6$ monotone
$0\! \to\!1$ words

$$|H_{2}|=n+1+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}i(n-i)
      =6+20=26,
\qquad
N(n)=n+1+\frac{n(n-1)(n+1)}{6} ,
$$

is the number of distinct positive-strand haplotypes that can be made by
two successive orientation-fixed one-crossover meioses.  The six
monotone $F_{1}$ haplotypes are recovered for $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ and the
$20$ genuinely new $F_{3}$ haplotypes are the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$
with $0\le a<k<b\le5$, e.g. $10111,01011,00101,\dots$.  Up to order this
is the usual $26$–haplotype, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$\,26\cdot27/2=351\,$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen
strand.  Removing the two parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ haplotypes the
strictly new $F_{3}$ positive-strand haplotypes are the $20$ words with
one $1\to0$ descent, $24$ novel haplotypes together with the two
parents.  The $2^{5}=32$ binary words are not all reached; the two
four-switch words $01010,10101$ need three successive one-crossover
meioses.  If the $k=0,5$ formal no-crossover ends are discarded the
obligatory one-crossover interior set is the $0\!\to\!1$ family
$0\,***1$, $2^{3}=8$ haplotypes $01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,
01101,00101$, $36$ unordered diploid genotypes, the $11$ per phase
$\sum_{k\le2}\binom{4}{k}=11$ and $22$ two-phase counts often quoted in
the $t$–break literature.  This is the source of the $11/22/26/30$
discrepancy in the room. ∎
reflection_text.8:
The discussion is split on the book-keeping of degenerate crossovers and on whether the F1 pool is taken to be the four internal 0→1 mosaics or the six monotone
0^t1^{5-t}, t=0…5.

With the orientation fixed on the arbitrarily chosen + strand the first meiosis
on the heterozygote P0=00000 / P1=11111 is

rec_k(P0,P1)=0^k1^{5-k}, 0≤k≤5

on the + strand.  Putting h_a=0^{a}1^{5-a}, h_b=0^{b}1^{5-b}∈S1 the
F2→F3 gamete is

rec_k(h_a,h_b)[i]=h_a[i] i≤k , h_b[i] i>k .

Hence on the + strand

rec_k(h_a,h_b)=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},
m=min(a,k),

so that, apart from the monotone case b≤k, the non-trivial product is

h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a<k<b≤5 .

Up to order the word is uniquely determined by the triple
(a,k,b).  With the degenerate ends 0≤k≤5 the three numbers can be
chosen as three distinct elements of {0,…,5}.  Hence

N_mon = n+1 =6
N_1down = C(n+1,3)=C(6,3)=20

distinct + strand haplotypes are obtainable by two orientation-fixed
prefix–suffix replacements,

|H₂|=(n+1)+C(n+1,3)=6+20=26

i.e. the six monotone 0^t1^{5-t} and the 20 words
0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a<k<b≤5, e.g. 10111, 01011, 00101, …
In unordered diploid terms this is H(H+1)/2 =26·27/2=351 genotypes,
676 ordered pairs.  Removing the two parental haplotypes this is the
20 genuinely new two-breakpoint + strand mosaics quoted by Colleagues
1,3,5,6,10.

If the degenerate k=0,5 crossovers are excluded, i.e. an obligatory
internal crossover in every meiosis, the F1 pool is
G1={0^k1^{5-k}:1≤k≤4} and every F2→F3 gamete necessarily starts with 0
and ends with 1.  The reachable + strand set is then the 2^{n-2}=2^{3}=8
words 0 x_{2..4}1,

{01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101},

four of which are the F1 gametes and four are the new

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the strand convention fixed on the arbitrarily positive strand the founders are

P0=00000 , P1=11111

and a first meiosis on P0/P1 can only produce on this strand the monotone
thresholds

H1 = {0^t 1^{5-t} : 0≤t≤5} , |H1|=6 .

That is the whole F1 gamete pool on the positive strand.  Indeed an
orientation-fixed single crossover in a heterozygote h_a/h_b gives

rec_k(h_a,h_b) = h_a[1:k] h_b[k+1:5] , 0≤k≤5,

so with h_a,h_b∈H1 the gamete is monotone in each parent.

Now an F2 individual is h_a/h_b with h_a,h_b∈H1 and its gamete to F3 is
again rec_k(h_a,h_b) with the same orientation.  Write h_a=0^{a}1^{5-a},
h_b=0^{b}1^{5-b}.  Up to k=0,5

rec_k(h_a,h_b)=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},   m=min(a,k) ≤k≤b .

Hence on the positive strand a second-generation gamete is

h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} , 0≤a<k<b≤5,

i.e. at most one 1→0 descent, the descent that can be created at the
junction k→k+1.  The triple a,k,b is uniquely recoverable from the word:
a is the length of the initial 0-run, k the end of the first 1-run and b
the end of the second 0-run.

The six monotone words 0^t1^{5-t} are recovered for a≥k or k≥b.  The
genuinely new words are obtained for 0≤a<k<b≤5.  There are

C(6,3)=20

such triples, and with the six thresholds

|H2| = (n+1)+C(n+1,3) =6+20=26

different positive-strand haplotypes can be present in an F3 gamete
and hence in an F3 chromosome.  Explicitly the 20 new mosaics are the
0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} words, e.g. 10111,10011,…,00101,00010, the
six monotone founders being 11111,01111,…,00000.

In diploid terms this is 26² ordered pairs, 26·27/2=351 unordered
genotypes on the positive strand.

The 30-string count that is quoted in the switch literature is 
Nmax=2∑_{i=0}^{3}C(4,i)=30, i.e. all binary words of length five except
01010 and 10101.  That count is obtained only if the reciprocal
1→0 orientation is admitted as a distinct first-meiosis product, 
i.e. if H1 is taken as the 10 monotone 0→1 and 1→0 words.  The problem
states “sufficient asymmetry of the strands to allow recombination in
only one orientation’’ and “considering only the arbitrarily positive
strand”.  Under that stated asymmetry the 1→0 first-meiosis products
are not realizable on the positive strand, so the mirror half of the
30 set is excluded.  The remaining 0→1 half is precisely the 26 words
above, and the conventional t-break 22 count is the further restriction
to at most two switches on a fixed parental background.  With the
orientation fixed the attainable positive-strand haplotype pool in F3
is 26.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand the founder haplotypes are $P_{0}=00000$ and $P_{1}=11111$ and strand asymmetry is stated to allow recombination in only one orientation. With the sign convention used for the positive strand a single meiosis in $P_{0}/P_{1}$ therefore produces only the monotone $A\to B$ mosaics

$$H_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}=\{00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111\},$$

$|H_{1}|=6$, the six $F_{1}$ gametes.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is an element of $H_{1}$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is the orientation-fixed single cross-over product of two $H_{1}$ haplotypes $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$ and $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\,i\le k,\qquad {\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\,i>k,$$
$0\le k\le5$.  Up to $k=0,5$ this is

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad m=\min(a,k),$$

so on the fixed positive strand a second-generation gamete is $0$ up to the first $1\to0$ descent and then up again, i.e. at most one descent $1\to0$ can be created.  In binary form the reachable words are exactly the $0\to1$ words with $\le1$ descent, $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.

The six monotone thresholds are $a=k$ or $k=b$.  With $0\le a<k<b\le5$ the triple $(a,k,b)$ is uniquely recovered from the word, and the number of genuinely new words is $\binom{6}{3}=20$.  Explicitly

* monotone: $11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$;
* one descent: $10111,10011,10001,10000,11011,11001,11000,01011,01001,01000,11101,11100,01101,01100,00101,00100,11110,01110,00110,00010$.

Hence the positive-strand haplotype pool that can be present in a gamete, and therefore in a chromosome, of an $F_{3}$ individual is

$$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$$

distinct $0\to1$ strings, $6$ $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20$ new two-break mosaics.  The $2\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{4}{i}=30$ count is the maximal combinatorial set obtained if the $1\to0$ phase is counted as distinct on the same strand, i.e. if the reciprocal orientation is admitted.  With the stated strand asymmetry that reciprocal phase is not realised on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand, so $30$ is a double count of phase. The strand-asymmetric, orientation-fixed $F_{3}$ repertoire is the $26$ positive-strand haplotypes above, $351$ unordered diploid genotypes.

1.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write $0$ for the $A$ allele and $1$ for
the $B$ allele and put

$$
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{\,5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le 4 ,
$$

for the $F_{1}$ gamete which is obtained from $A=00000/B=11111$ by one
obligatory cross over in one of the $4$ inter-marker intervals.  Up to
the sign convention this is the whole $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the
$+$ strand

$$
S_{1}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad |S_{1}|=4,
$$

the two formal ends $k=0,5$ being the parental chromosomes.  Let an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis be a prefix–suffix cut

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i]\;i\le k,\qquad
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}[i]\;i>k ,
$$

$1\le k\le 4$, $h_{a},h_{b}\in S_{1}$.  Then

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{i}=0\iff 
i\le\min(a,k)\ {\rm or}\ k<i\le b ,
$$

so that every $F_{3}$ gamete still begins with $0$ and ends with $1$.
Writing $w_{2}w_{3}w_{4}$ for the three interior sites we have

$$
w_{i}=
\begin{cases}
h_{a}[i]&i\le k\\
h_{b}[i]&i>k
\end{cases}
$$

and the three interior sites can be chosen independently.  Hence on
the fixed $0\to1$ orientation the $F_{3}$ gamete pool is

$$
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{\,0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1\;:\;x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\bigl\{0xxx1\bigr\},
$$

i.e. the $2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ positive-strand chromosomes

$$
\begin{aligned}
&01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\\
&01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,
\end{aligned}
$$

the four $k_{F1}=1\ldots4$ monotone $F_{1}$ words being recovered as the
special cases $x_{2}=x_{3}=x_{4}=0$ and the four words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ being the first genuine two-meiosis
recombinants.  In particular the $F_{3}$ gamete pool on the chosen
strand is the $0\ldots1$ family $2^{\,n-2}$ with $n=5$.

Up to order the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random in an $F_{3}$
zygote, $H^{2}=64$ ordered and

$$
N_{g}=\binom{H+1}{2}= \frac{8\times 9}{2}=36
$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes, the $8$ haplotypes above being the
distinct $+$–strand chromosome sequences that can be seen in the $F_{3}$
generation.  The $6$ formal monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$,
are recovered if the $k=0,5$ telomeric cuts are admitted as formal
recombinants.  With the $k=0,5$ ends kept the $+$–strand pool is
$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct chromosomes,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
genotypes, the $20$ new words being the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$0\le a<k<b\le5$, usually quoted as the two-generation one-crossover
bound.  This is the $26$–haplotype, $351$–genotype convention often
quoted in the literature. ∎

2.text:
On the $+$ strand we can write the two founders as

$$
A=0^{5}=00000 ,\qquad B=1^{5}=11111
$$

and write a first generation gamete as the monotone $0\to1$ mosaic

$$
h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le 5 .
$$

With the one orientation asymmetry a meiosis is the prefix–suffix
operation

$$
 {\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]\,h_{b}[k+1:5],
\qquad 1\le k\le 4 ,
$$

so that a gamete is always $0\ldots1$ on the $+$ strand.  With an
obligatory interior break the $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand is

$$
{\cal S}_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le 4\}
   =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},
$$

four haplotypes, the two founders $0^{5},1^{5}$ never being made by a
genuine crossover.

Let $x=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $y=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ be the
two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k\in
\{1,2,3,4\}$.  Then

$$
z_{i}= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
x_{i},&i\le k\\[1mm]
y_{i},&i>k
\end{array}\right.
$$

is $z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ and $z_{2},z_{3},z_{4}$ are completely free.
Writing $z=0\,u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}\,1$,

$$
u_{i}\in\{0,1\},\qquad 2\le i\le4,
$$

is obtained e.g. from $a\le k<b$ with

$$
z=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},
$$

and every $0u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}1$ is realised.  Hence on the arbitrarily
chosen $+$ strand the $F_{3}$ gamete pool is

$$
{\cal H}_{2}=\{0xxx1:x\in\{0,1\}^{3}\}
$$

the $2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ chromosomes

$$
\begin{array}{llll}
01111,&00111,&00011,&00001,\\
01011,&01001,&01101,&00101,
\end{array}
$$

the four monotone $F_{1}$ products together with the four
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ three–switch mosaics $01011,01001,01101,00101$.
In particular the three interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$.

Up to order this is $H(H+1)/2$ diploid autosomes,
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered $F_{3}$ genotypes, $8^{2}=64$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs, on the chosen strand.  The four $F_{1}$ haplotypes
are recovered as the special cases $k\to a$ or $k\to b$.

Remark.  If the telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ are admitted as a
recombination the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone words
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the two-step prefix–suffix set on the
$+$ strand is $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,
$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes,
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes, the $20$
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<k<b\le5$, being the genuinely new
two–break mosaics.  This is the usual $26$-haplotype, $351$-genotype
formal count. ∎

6.text:
On the strand which is kept fixed the two homozygous founders can be
written

* $A=0^{5}$ , $B=1^{5}$

on the $+$ strand.  A single orientation fixed meiosis in the
$A/B$ heterozygote can only make the monotone mosaics

\begin{equation*}
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{\,5-a},\qquad 0\le a\le 5 ,
\end{equation*}
the $a$th marker being the last $0$ of the gamete.  With an obligatory
one break per gamete the $k=0,5$ formal non-recombinants are discarded
and

\begin{equation*}
H_{1}^{+}=\{h_{a}:1\le a\le 4\}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},
\end{equation*}
four $0\to 1$ gametes, the $F_{1}$ gamete pool.  An $F_{2}$ plant is
$h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  With a single obligatory break
at $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ on the $+$ strand

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=
h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad h_{b}(i),\;i>k ,
\end{equation*}
so that on the $+$ strand

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad m=\min (a,k) .
\end{equation*}
Hence
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ is always $0\ldots 1$ on the $+$ strand.
It is monotone iff $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ and it is genuinely
two-break iff

\begin{equation*}
a<k<b ,
\end{equation*}
in which case

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad 1\le a<k<b\le4 .
\end{equation*}
For $n=5$ the $0\to1$ words are exactly the $2^{\,n-2}$ words which
start with $0$ and end with $1$.  With $a<k<b$ there are
$\binom{4}{3}=4$ genuinely new mosaics,

\begin{aligned}
(1,2,3)&:01011\\
(1,2,4)&:01001\\
(1,3,4)&:01101\\
(2,3,4)&:00101,
\end{aligned}
i.e. the four three–run $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ words, and the four
monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words

$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001$,

so that on the arbitrarily chosen orientation the $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$
gamete pool is

\begin{equation*}
H_{2}^{+}=\{0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
\end{equation*}
the $2^{3}=8$ $0\ldots1$ strings.  In particular the three interior
SNPs are free in the $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ string can ever be seen
on the fixed $+$ strand.  Up to order the diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes
that can be made from the eight $+$ –strand haplotypes are

\begin{equation*}
N_{d}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36
\end{equation*}
unordered, $8^{2}=64$ ordered, diploid genotypes.  The four
monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes, the four
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ words are the new two–break recombinants
first seen in the $F_{3}$.

Remark.  If the formal $k=0,5$ non–recombinant ends are kept in the
count the $+$–strand $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{a}1^{5-a},\,0\le a\le5$.  Two successive orientation–fixed
one–break meioses then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one
$1\to0$ descent,

\begin{equation*}
H_{2}^{+,*}= \{0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}:0\le a<k<b\le5\},
\end{equation*}
$|H_{2}^{+,*}|=n+1+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}i(n-i)=6+20=26$ distinct
$+$–strand haplotypes, $6$ monotone $F_{1}$ haplotypes and the
$20=\binom{6}{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants, $26^{2}=676$
ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the
chosen strand.  Discarding the formal $k=0,5$ ends this is the $2^{3}=8$
$0\ldots1$ haplotypes quoted above. ∎

9.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write the two founders as

* $P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$ ,

and write a first–meiosis gamete as the monotone word

$$
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 0\le a\le 5 ,
\tag{1}
$$

the $0\to1$ threshold which is obtained by a single orientation fixed
cut.  With the convention $k=0,5$ for the two telomeric cuts the $F_{1}$
pool is $H_{1}=\{h_{a}\}$, $|H_{1}|=6$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is
the orientation fixed prefix–suffix product

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=
\begin{cases}
h_{a}(i),&i\le k\\[1mm]
h_{b}(i),&i>k
\end{cases}
\qquad 0\le k\le5,
\tag{2}
$$

$h_{a},h_{b}\in H_{1}$.  Putting $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})
 =0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,\max(0,b-k)}1^{\,5-\max(b,k)} .
\tag{3}
$$

If $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ the product is again a threshold $0^{t}1^{5-t}$,
$t\in\{0,\dots ,5\}$.  The genuinely new words are obtained for

$$
a<k<b ,
$$

$$
h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad
0\le a<k<b\le5 ,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. a word with an initial $0$–run of length $a$, a first $1$–run
ending at $k$ and a second $0$–run ending at $b$.  The triple
$(a,k,b)$ is read off uniquely from the word, so distinct triples give
distinct words.  The number of triples is

$$
N_{1}(n)=\#\{0\le a<k<b\le n\}=\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

and with the $n+1$ monotone thresholds the positive–strand pool which
can be carried by an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is

$$
|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}
      =\frac{(n+1)\bigl(n^{2}-n+6\bigr)}{6},
$$

the familiar concatenation of two monotone words.  For $n=5$

$$
|H_{2}|=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26
$$

different $0\to1$ haplotypes on the chosen strand, $6$ of them the
$F_{1}$ thresholds

$$
11111,\;01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\;00000,
$$

and the $20=\binom63$ words

$$
0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,
$$

e.g. $10111,10011,\dots ,00010$, the $20$ words which contain exactly
one $1\to0$ descent.  In particular there are $20$ genuinely new
positive–strand haplotypes in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool, $24$ new
haplotypes together with the two founders.  The $26$ haplotypes can be
paired at random in an $F_{3}$ diploid, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and

$$
N_{g}=\frac{|H_{2}|\bigl(|H_{2}|+1\bigr)}2=\frac{26\times27}{2}=351
$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed strand.

Remark on the strict “exactly one internal cross over’’ convention.
If the telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded the $F_{1}$ pool is
$h_{a}$ with $1\le a\le4$, $|H_{1}^{i}|=4$, and (4) is restricted to
$1\le a<k<b\le4$.  There are then $\binom43=4$ non–monotone words

$$
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,
$$

together with the four monotone $F_{1}$ words $01111,00111,00011,
00001$, i.e. $8=2^{\,3}$ distinct $0\ldots1$ positive–strand
haplotypes which can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome, $4+4$ new
words.  Unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes are $8\cdot9/2=36$, $64$
ordered, the $2^{\,n-2}$ bound usually quoted for one internal
crossover per meiosis on a fixed strand.  The $26$–haplotype, $351$–
genotype count above is the conventional $k=0,5$ inclusive count and
is the $N(n)=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ bound normally quoted for two
successive orientation–fixed single–crossover meioses. ∎

8.text:
On the strand which is kept the two founders are

$P_{0}=0^{5}\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

on the $+$ strand.  With an obligatory internal break the $F_{1}$ gamete
which is ever recovered on the $+$ strand is

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le 4 ,$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,  the $k=0,5$ telomeric “recombinants’’
being absent.  Every $F_{2}$ plant is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.
A $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is on the $+$ strand

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=
\begin{cases}
h_{a}(i), &i\le k\\
h_{b}(i), &i>k
\end{cases}\qquad 1\le k\le4 ,$

so that

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b} $

for $a<k<b$ and $0^{\ell}1^{5-\ell}$ otherwise.  In particular
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ and
the three interior sites $2,3,4$ can be chosen independently of one
another.  Putting $k=1$

${\rm rec}_{1}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{1}h_{b}[2\!:\!5]$

gives the four $F_{1}$ words,  $k=2$ gives

$0\,h_{a}[2]\,h_{b}[3]\,h_{b}[4]\,1$,

$k=3$ gives $0\,h_{a}[2]\,h_{a}[3]\,h_{b}[4]\,1$ and $k=4$ gives
$0\,h_{a}[2]\,h_{a}[3]\,h_{a}[4]\,1$.  Hence, up to the fixed
$0\ldots1$ phase,

$\;{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}=\{\,0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\;:\;x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}\;,$

i.e. $2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$–strand chromosomes, namely

$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$,

four of them being the $F_{1}$ gametes and four

$01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$

the genuinely new two-breakpoint $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ mosaics which
are first seen in the $F_{3}$.  In diploid terms the $8$ haplotypes can
be paired arbitrarily, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\,8+{8\choose2}=36$ 
unordered $F_{3}$ zygotes on the chosen strand, $16$ haplotypes and
$2\times11$ $=22$ haplotypes $11$ per phase if the reciprocal $1\to0$
phase is restored.

*Remark.*  If the telomeric formal recombinations $k=0,5$ are retained
as the usual textbook book-keeping the $F_{1}$ pool is
$0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$ and the $+$–strand set obtainable by two
orientation-fixed prefix–suffix replacements is

$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$0\le a<k<b\le5$, $20$ of them new in the $F_{3}$, $26^{2}=676$ ordered
and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid genotypes.  The $8$ haplotypes
above are the physically strict obligatory-internal-crossover
realisation of that set, the $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ six-word set being recovered
once the degenerate $k=0,5$ ends are admitted. ∎

5.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand the two founders can be written as

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5} ,$$

and with the strand asymmetry we may write a first meiosis gamete as the
monotone mosaic

$$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le 5,$$

i.e. $H_{1}=\{00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111\}$ with
$|H_{1}|=n+1=6$.  Up to the trivial $k=0,5$ ends an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
gamete is the orientation fixed prefix–suffix

$${\rm rec}_{k}\!\left(h_{a},h_{b}\right)[i]=
\begin{cases}
h_{a}(i),&i\le k\\
h_{b}(i),&i>k
\end{cases},\qquad 0\le k\le5,$$

so that with $m=\min (a,k)$

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad m\le k .$$

Hence on the $+$ strand a word is of the form

$$0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad
0\le a\le k\le b\le5, $$

i.e. a binary word of length $5$ with at most one $1\to0$ descent.
The monotone $c_{0}$ words are

$$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad t=0\ldots5, $$

six of them.  For a descent at the position $i$, $1\le i\le4$, the
initial $0$–run can be chosen in $i$ ways and the final $1$–run in
$5-i$ ways, so that

$$N_{1}(i)=i(5-i),\qquad
N_{1}=\sum_{i=1}^{4}i(5-i)=4+6+6+4=20 ,$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Apart from the six monotone
$F_{1}$ haplotypes we therefore obtain

$$\binom{6}{3}=20$$

genuinely new $F_{3}$ mosaics

$$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 
0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

e.g.  $01011,00101,01101,\dots$ The positive–strand haplotype pool
which can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete is therefore

$$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,
\qquad n=5, $$

$6$ monotone $F_{1}$ words and $20$ two–meiosis mosaics.  In closed
form

$$N(n)=\frac{(n+1)\bigl(n^{2}-n+6\bigr)}6, $$

$N(5)=26$.  The six monotone words are the ordinary $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$
set; the $20$ words $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$
are the new $F_{3}$ recombinants on the $+$ strand.  Up to order the
$H_{2}=26$ haplotypes can be paired, giving

$$N_{g}^{\rm ord}=H_{2}^{2}=676,\qquad 
N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\frac{H_{2}(H_{2}+1)}2=
\frac{26\times27}{2}=351 $$

ordered, resp. unordered, diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the $6$ monotone
haplotypes being the ordinary $F_{2}$ set.

In the strict interior–crossover convention $k,a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ the
trivial telomeric $k=0,5$ ends are removed.  The monotone core is then
$\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ and the non–monotone core is

$$\{01011,01001,01101,00101\}, $$

i.e. $4+4=8$ distinct $0\ldots1$ positive–strand haplotypes,
$2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the $20$ words quoted above being the
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ core with the $k=0,5$ ends admitted.  This
is the $26$ haplotype $=351$ genotype inclusive statement usually
quoted; the $8$–haplotype $=36$ genotype set is the genuine interior
one–crossover per meiosis core. ∎

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand the two inbred founders can be written as

$P_{0}=00000$ , $P_{1}=11111$ 

and with the strand asymmetry fixed the only product of a single
crossover between two homologues $x$ and $y$ on the $+$ strand is

${\rm rec}_{k}(x,y)=\;x[1\!:\!k]\,y[k+1\!:\!5]\qquad 1\le k\le 4 ,
$

the $k=0,5$ products being the formal no-crossover limits.  
The $F_{1}$ is $P_{0}/P_{1}$ so that its gametes, i.e. the chromosomes
which are present in the $F_{2}$, are the obligatory one-break
$0\to 1$ mosaics

${\cal H}_{1}=\Big\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;,\;1\le k\le4\Big\}
     =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ ,
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=4$.
Up to the fixed orientation the $F_{1}$ zygote is $P_{0}/P_{1}$; the
first recombinant chromosomes appear in the $F_{2}$.

Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cross over at $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  Then on the
$+$ strand

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
\begin{cases}
0^{b}1^{5-b}, &k\le a,\;b\ge k\\
0^{k}1^{5-k}, &b<k\le a\\
0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},&a<k<b ,
\end{cases}
$

i.e. a gamete is monotone $0^{b}1^{5-b}$ or $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ or
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $1\le a<k<b\le4$.  Hence every
$F_{3}$ chromosome is $0$ on the leftmost marker and $1$ on the rightmost
marker and the three interior markers are free.  In fact

$\begin{array}{lll}
k=1:&01111,00111,00011,00001\\
k=2:&01111,01011,01001,00111,00011,00001\\
k=3:&01111,01101,00111,00101,00011,00001\\
k=4:&01111,00111,00011,00001
\end{array}
$

so that, on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation,

${\cal H}_{2}=\{0\,x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}\,1\;:\;x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101\}$

is the whole $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete pool.  Up to the chosen orientation
$|{\cal H}_{2}|=2^{\,5-2}=8$ distinct positive-strand haplotypes can be
present in an $F_{3}$ individual, the four $F_{2}$ one-break haplotypes
being contained in the set.  They are exactly the $0xxx1$ words, i.e.
the three interior SNPs are free.  In diploid terms the unordered
genotypes obtainable from the eight haplotypes are

$N_{g}=\binom{|{\cal H}_{2}|+1}{2}=8\cdot9/2=36$,

$64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs, $8^{2}=64$ ordered pairs.

In particular the $F_{3}$ positive-strand repertoire is the $2^{\,n-2}$
$0\ldots1$ family.  If the formal telomeric cross-overs $k=0,5$ are
admitted as recombination events the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the
six monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the two-step
prefix-suffix construction gives the usual inclusive count

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{\rm inc}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct $0\to1$ haplotypes on the fixed strand, $26^{2}=676$ ordered
and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the $20$
non-monotone words $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<k<b\le5$, being
the genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants.  The $8$–haplotype count above
is the $k=1\ldots4$ obligatory-crossover, strictly internal, version of
the same construction. ∎

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand put the two founders

$$P_{0}=0^{5}\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$$

and write a first meiosis product in the $0\to 1$ phase as

$$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le5 ,$$

the $6$ monotone words

$H_{1}=\{11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000\}$ .

A second meiosis product on the same strand is the ordinary
prefix–suffix recombination

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i)\;i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i)\;i>k$ ,

$0\le k\le5$, $h_{a},h_{b}\in H_{1}$.  Putting $m=\min (a,k)$ one gets

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}\qquad
m\le k,\;b\ge k,  $$

i.e. up to the trivial $k=0,5$ ends

$$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad
0\le a<k<b\le5 , $$

the words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  For a fixed $k$

$N_{1}(k)=k\,(5-k)$

different non–monotone words are obtained and

$$N_{1}=\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20
$$

words have the form $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.
Together with the $n+1=6$ monotone $F_{1}$ words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ this is

$$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\frac{n(n-1)(n+1)}{6}
       =6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$$

different positive–strand haplotypes which can be carried by an $F_{3}$
gamete and hence by an $F_{3}$ chromosome.  The six monotone words are
the $F_{1}$ gametes

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$

and the $20$ genuinely new $F_{3}$ words are e.g.

$10111,10011,10001,10000,11011,11001,11000,01011,\dots ,11110,
01110,00110,00010$,

the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ words with $a<k<b$.  In unordered
diploid terms this is

$$N_{g}=\frac{|H_{2}|(|H_{2}|+1)}2=
\frac{26\times27}{2}=351$$

different $F_{3}$ autosomes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal
pairs.  The $20$ words are the $F_{3}$-specific recombinants; with the
two parental haplotypes removed the usual statement is $24$ new
positive–strand haplotypes, $20$ of them strictly new in the $F_{3}$.

Remark.  If a crossover is required in every meiosis, $k=0,5$ is
formally excluded, $S_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}$, and the
$F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ products are the $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ words
$0\,x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}1$, $x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$, i.e. $01111,00111,00011,
00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$.  This is the $8$ haplotype,
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid, obligate-crossover limit, the $26$
haplotype count above being the conventional $k=0,5$-inclusive
$ (n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count. ∎

public_text.7:
With the strand convention fixed on the arbitrarily positive strand the founders are

P0=00000 , P1=11111

and a first meiosis on P0/P1 can only produce on this strand the monotone
thresholds

H1 = {0^t 1^{5-t} : 0≤t≤5} , |H1|=6 .

That is the whole F1 gamete pool on the positive strand.  Indeed an
orientation-fixed single crossover in a heterozygote h_a/h_b gives

rec_k(h_a,h_b) = h_a[1:k] h_b[k+1:5] , 0≤k≤5,

so with h_a,h_b∈H1 the gamete is monotone in each parent.

Now an F2 individual is h_a/h_b with h_a,h_b∈H1 and its gamete to F3 is
again rec_k(h_a,h_b) with the same orientation.  Write h_a=0^{a}1^{5-a},
h_b=0^{b}1^{5-b}.  Up to k=0,5

rec_k(h_a,h_b)=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},   m=min(a,k) ≤k≤b .

Hence on the positive strand a second-generation gamete is

h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} , 0≤a<k<b≤5,

i.e. at most one 1→0 descent, the descent that can be created at the
junction k→k+1.  The triple a,k,b is uniquely recoverable from the word:
a is the length of the initial 0-run, k the end of the first 1-run and b
the end of the second 0-run.

The six monotone words 0^t1^{5-t} are recovered for a≥k or k≥b.  The
genuinely new words are obtained for 0≤a<k<b≤5.  There are

C(6,3)=20

such triples, and with the six thresholds

|H2| = (n+1)+C(n+1,3) =6+20=26

different positive-strand haplotypes can be present in an F3 gamete
and hence in an F3 chromosome.  Explicitly the 20 new mosaics are the
0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} words, e.g. 10111,10011,…,00101,00010, the
six monotone founders being 11111,01111,…,00000.

In diploid terms this is 26² ordered pairs, 26·27/2=351 unordered
genotypes on the positive strand.

The 30-string count that is quoted in the switch literature is 
Nmax=2∑_{i=0}^{3}C(4,i)=30, i.e. all binary words of length five except
01010 and 10101.  That count is obtained only if the reciprocal
1→0 orientation is admitted as a distinct first-meiosis product, 
i.e. if H1 is taken as the 10 monotone 0→1 and 1→0 words.  The problem
states “sufficient asymmetry of the strands to allow recombination in
only one orientation’’ and “considering only the arbitrarily positive
strand”.  Under that stated asymmetry the 1→0 first-meiosis products
are not realizable on the positive strand, so the mirror half of the
30 set is excluded.  The remaining 0→1 half is precisely the 26 words
above, and the conventional t-break 22 count is the further restriction
to at most two switches on a fixed parental background.  With the
orientation fixed the attainable positive-strand haplotype pool in F3
is 26.
public_text.10:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand the founder haplotypes are $P_{0}=00000$ and $P_{1}=11111$ and strand asymmetry is stated to allow recombination in only one orientation. With the sign convention used for the positive strand a single meiosis in $P_{0}/P_{1}$ therefore produces only the monotone $A\to B$ mosaics

$$H_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}=\{00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111\},$$

$|H_{1}|=6$, the six $F_{1}$ gametes.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is an element of $H_{1}$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is the orientation-fixed single cross-over product of two $H_{1}$ haplotypes $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$ and $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\,i\le k,\qquad {\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\,i>k,$$
$0\le k\le5$.  Up to $k=0,5$ this is

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad m=\min(a,k),$$

so on the fixed positive strand a second-generation gamete is $0$ up to the first $1\to0$ descent and then up again, i.e. at most one descent $1\to0$ can be created.  In binary form the reachable words are exactly the $0\to1$ words with $\le1$ descent, $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.

The six monotone thresholds are $a=k$ or $k=b$.  With $0\le a<k<b\le5$ the triple $(a,k,b)$ is uniquely recovered from the word, and the number of genuinely new words is $\binom{6}{3}=20$.  Explicitly

* monotone: $11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$;
* one descent: $10111,10011,10001,10000,11011,11001,11000,01011,01001,01000,11101,11100,01101,01100,00101,00100,11110,01110,00110,00010$.

Hence the positive-strand haplotype pool that can be present in a gamete, and therefore in a chromosome, of an $F_{3}$ individual is

$$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$$

distinct $0\to1$ strings, $6$ $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20$ new two-break mosaics.  The $2\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{4}{i}=30$ count is the maximal combinatorial set obtained if the $1\to0$ phase is counted as distinct on the same strand, i.e. if the reciprocal orientation is admitted.  With the stated strand asymmetry that reciprocal phase is not realised on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand, so $30$ is a double count of phase.  Likewise the conventional $2\sum_{k\le2}\binom{4}{k}=22$ figure is the $t$-break per lineage count and excludes recombination of two first-generation recombinants, which is exactly what occurs in the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis.  The strand-asymmetric, orientation-fixed $F_{3}$ repertoire is the $26$ positive-strand haplotypes above, $351$ unordered diploid genotypes.
public_text.1:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write $0$ for the $A$ allele and $1$ for
the $B$ allele and put

$$
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{\,5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le 4 ,
$$

for the $F_{1}$ gamete which is obtained from $A=00000/B=11111$ by one
obligatory cross over in one of the $4$ inter-marker intervals.  Up to
the sign convention this is the whole $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the
$+$ strand

$$
S_{1}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad |S_{1}|=4,
$$

the two formal ends $k=0,5$ being the parental chromosomes.  Let an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis be a prefix–suffix cut

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i]\;i\le k,\qquad
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}[i]\;i>k ,
$$

$1\le k\le 4$, $h_{a},h_{b}\in S_{1}$.  Then

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{i}=0\iff 
i\le\min(a,k)\ {\rm or}\ k<i\le b ,
$$

so that every $F_{3}$ gamete still begins with $0$ and ends with $1$.
Writing $w_{2}w_{3}w_{4}$ for the three interior sites we have

$$
w_{i}=
\begin{cases}
h_{a}[i]&i\le k\\
h_{b}[i]&i>k
\end{cases}
$$

and the three interior sites can be chosen independently.  Hence on
the fixed $0\to1$ orientation the $F_{3}$ gamete pool is

$$
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{\,0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1\;:\;x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\bigl\{0xxx1\bigr\},
$$

i.e. the $2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ positive-strand chromosomes

$$
\begin{aligned}
&01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\\
&01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,
\end{aligned}
$$

the four $k_{F1}=1\ldots4$ monotone $F_{1}$ words being recovered as the
special cases $x_{2}=x_{3}=x_{4}=0$ and the four words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ being the first genuine two-meiosis
recombinants.  In particular the $F_{3}$ gamete pool on the chosen
strand is the $0\ldots1$ family $2^{\,n-2}$ with $n=5$.

Up to order the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random in an $F_{3}$
zygote, $H^{2}=64$ ordered and

$$
N_{g}=\binom{H+1}{2}= \frac{8\times 9}{2}=36
$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes, the $8$ haplotypes above being the
distinct $+$–strand chromosome sequences that can be seen in the $F_{3}$
generation.  The $6$ formal monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$,
are recovered if the $k=0,5$ telomeric cuts are admitted as formal
recombinants.  With the $k=0,5$ ends kept the $+$–strand pool is
$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct chromosomes,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
genotypes, the $20$ new words being the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$0\le a<k<b\le5$, usually quoted as the two-generation one-crossover
bound.  This is the $26$–haplotype, $351$–genotype convention often
quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.2:
On the $+$ strand we can write the two founders as

$$
A=0^{5}=00000 ,\qquad B=1^{5}=11111
$$

and write a first generation gamete as the monotone $0\to1$ mosaic

$$
h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le 5 .
$$

With the one orientation asymmetry a meiosis is the prefix–suffix
operation

$$
 {\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]\,h_{b}[k+1:5],
\qquad 1\le k\le 4 ,
$$

so that a gamete is always $0\ldots1$ on the $+$ strand.  With an
obligatory interior break the $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand is

$$
{\cal S}_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le 4\}
   =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},
$$

four haplotypes, the two founders $0^{5},1^{5}$ never being made by a
genuine crossover.

Let $x=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $y=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ be the
two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k\in
\{1,2,3,4\}$.  Then

$$
z_{i}= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
x_{i},&i\le k\\[1mm]
y_{i},&i>k
\end{array}\right.
$$

is $z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ and $z_{2},z_{3},z_{4}$ are completely free.
Writing $z=0\,u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}\,1$,

$$
u_{i}\in\{0,1\},\qquad 2\le i\le4,
$$

is obtained e.g. from $a\le k<b$ with

$$
z=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},
$$

and every $0u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}1$ is realised.  Hence on the arbitrarily
chosen $+$ strand the $F_{3}$ gamete pool is

$$
{\cal H}_{2}=\{0xxx1:x\in\{0,1\}^{3}\}
$$

the $2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ chromosomes

$$
\begin{array}{llll}
01111,&00111,&00011,&00001,\\
01011,&01001,&01101,&00101,
\end{array}
$$

the four monotone $F_{1}$ products together with the four
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ three–switch mosaics $01011,01001,01101,00101$.
In particular the three interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$.

Up to order this is $H(H+1)/2$ diploid autosomes,
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered $F_{3}$ genotypes, $8^{2}=64$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs, on the chosen strand.  The four $F_{1}$ haplotypes
are recovered as the special cases $k\to a$ or $k\to b$.

Remark.  If the telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ are admitted as a
recombination the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone words
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the two-step prefix–suffix set on the
$+$ strand is $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,
$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes,
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes, the $20$
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<k<b\le5$, being the genuinely new
two–break mosaics.  This is the usual $26$-haplotype, $351$-genotype
formal count. ∎
public_text.6:
On the strand which is kept fixed the two homozygous founders can be
written

* $A=0^{5}$ , $B=1^{5}$

on the $+$ strand.  A single orientation fixed meiosis in the
$A/B$ heterozygote can only make the monotone mosaics

\begin{equation*}
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{\,5-a},\qquad 0\le a\le 5 ,
\end{equation*}
the $a$th marker being the last $0$ of the gamete.  With an obligatory
one break per gamete the $k=0,5$ formal non-recombinants are discarded
and

\begin{equation*}
H_{1}^{+}=\{h_{a}:1\le a\le 4\}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},
\end{equation*}
four $0\to 1$ gametes, the $F_{1}$ gamete pool.  An $F_{2}$ plant is
$h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  With a single obligatory break
at $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ on the $+$ strand

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=
h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad h_{b}(i),\;i>k ,
\end{equation*}
so that on the $+$ strand

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad m=\min (a,k) .
\end{equation*}
Hence
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ is always $0\ldots 1$ on the $+$ strand.
It is monotone iff $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ and it is genuinely
two-break iff

\begin{equation*}
a<k<b ,
\end{equation*}
in which case

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad 1\le a<k<b\le4 .
\end{equation*}
For $n=5$ the $0\to1$ words are exactly the $2^{\,n-2}$ words which
start with $0$ and end with $1$.  With $a<k<b$ there are
$\binom{4}{3}=4$ genuinely new mosaics,

\begin{aligned}
(1,2,3)&:01011\\
(1,2,4)&:01001\\
(1,3,4)&:01101\\
(2,3,4)&:00101,
\end{aligned}
i.e. the four three–run $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ words, and the four
monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words

$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001$,

so that on the arbitrarily chosen orientation the $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$
gamete pool is

\begin{equation*}
H_{2}^{+}=\{0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
\end{equation*}
the $2^{3}=8$ $0\ldots1$ strings.  In particular the three interior
SNPs are free in the $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ string can ever be seen
on the fixed $+$ strand.  Up to order the diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes
that can be made from the eight $+$ –strand haplotypes are

\begin{equation*}
N_{d}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36
\end{equation*}
unordered, $8^{2}=64$ ordered, diploid genotypes.  The four
monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes, the four
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ words are the new two–break recombinants
first seen in the $F_{3}$.

Remark.  If the formal $k=0,5$ non–recombinant ends are kept in the
count the $+$–strand $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{a}1^{5-a},\,0\le a\le5$.  Two successive orientation–fixed
one–break meioses then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one
$1\to0$ descent,

\begin{equation*}
H_{2}^{+,*}= \{0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}:0\le a<k<b\le5\},
\end{equation*}
$|H_{2}^{+,*}|=n+1+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}i(n-i)=6+20=26$ distinct
$+$–strand haplotypes, $6$ monotone $F_{1}$ haplotypes and the
$20=\binom{6}{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants, $26^{2}=676$
ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the
chosen strand.  Discarding the formal $k=0,5$ ends this is the $2^{3}=8$
$0\ldots1$ haplotypes quoted above. ∎
public_text.9:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write the two founders as

* $P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$ ,

and write a first–meiosis gamete as the monotone word

$$
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 0\le a\le 5 ,
\tag{1}
$$

the $0\to1$ threshold which is obtained by a single orientation fixed
cut.  With the convention $k=0,5$ for the two telomeric cuts the $F_{1}$
pool is $H_{1}=\{h_{a}\}$, $|H_{1}|=6$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is
the orientation fixed prefix–suffix product

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=
\begin{cases}
h_{a}(i),&i\le k\\[1mm]
h_{b}(i),&i>k
\end{cases}
\qquad 0\le k\le5,
\tag{2}
$$

$h_{a},h_{b}\in H_{1}$.  Putting $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})
 =0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,\max(0,b-k)}1^{\,5-\max(b,k)} .
\tag{3}
$$

If $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ the product is again a threshold $0^{t}1^{5-t}$,
$t\in\{0,\dots ,5\}$.  The genuinely new words are obtained for

$$
a<k<b ,
$$

$$
h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad
0\le a<k<b\le5 ,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. a word with an initial $0$–run of length $a$, a first $1$–run
ending at $k$ and a second $0$–run ending at $b$.  The triple
$(a,k,b)$ is read off uniquely from the word, so distinct triples give
distinct words.  The number of triples is

$$
N_{1}(n)=\#\{0\le a<k<b\le n\}=\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

and with the $n+1$ monotone thresholds the positive–strand pool which
can be carried by an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is

$$
|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}
      =\frac{(n+1)\bigl(n^{2}-n+6\bigr)}{6},
$$

the familiar concatenation of two monotone words.  For $n=5$

$$
|H_{2}|=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26
$$

different $0\to1$ haplotypes on the chosen strand, $6$ of them the
$F_{1}$ thresholds

$$
11111,\;01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\;00000,
$$

and the $20=\binom63$ words

$$
0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,
$$

e.g. $10111,10011,\dots ,00010$, the $20$ words which contain exactly
one $1\to0$ descent.  In particular there are $20$ genuinely new
positive–strand haplotypes in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool, $24$ new
haplotypes together with the two founders.  The $26$ haplotypes can be
paired at random in an $F_{3}$ diploid, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and

$$
N_{g}=\frac{|H_{2}|\bigl(|H_{2}|+1\bigr)}2=\frac{26\times27}{2}=351
$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed strand.

Remark on the strict “exactly one internal cross over’’ convention.
If the telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded the $F_{1}$ pool is
$h_{a}$ with $1\le a\le4$, $|H_{1}^{i}|=4$, and (4) is restricted to
$1\le a<k<b\le4$.  There are then $\binom43=4$ non–monotone words

$$
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,
$$

together with the four monotone $F_{1}$ words $01111,00111,00011,
00001$, i.e. $8=2^{\,3}$ distinct $0\ldots1$ positive–strand
haplotypes which can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome, $4+4$ new
words.  Unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes are $8\cdot9/2=36$, $64$
ordered, the $2^{\,n-2}$ bound usually quoted for one internal
crossover per meiosis on a fixed strand.  The $26$–haplotype, $351$–
genotype count above is the conventional $k=0,5$ inclusive count and
is the $N(n)=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ bound normally quoted for two
successive orientation–fixed single–crossover meioses. ∎
