reflection_text.5:
The positive strand is fixed to the $0\to1$ parental phase, $P_{0}=00000$, $P_{1}=11111$, and recombination is orientation-fixed. 
A first meiosis in $P_{0}/P_{1}$ therefore makes the monotone $0\to1$ thresholds
$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$. With an obligatory internal crossover the $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand is
$S_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$, $|S_{1}|=4$. 
The two formal telomeric products $k=0,5$ are $00000,11111$ and are not produced by a genuine crossover.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is the orientation-fixed prefix–suffix
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),i\le k$, $h_{b}(i),i>k$, $1\le k\le4$,
$a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  With $m=\min(a,k)$,
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ for $a<k<b$, otherwise monotone. 
Hence every $F_{3}$ gamete is $0\ldots1$ on the chosen strand and the three interior markers
$2,3,4$ are free.  Up to the fixed $0\to1$ phase

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand haplotypes

$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$,

four monotone $F_{1}$ products and four genuine two-meiosis mosaics
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.  Unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes from these $H=8$ haplotypes are
$H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$, $H^{2}=64$ ordered.

If the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are admitted as book-keeping non-recombinants the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone thresholds
$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},0\le t\le5$, $|H_{1}|=6$.  Two successive orientation-fixed single cuts then give the
$0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$.  The genuinely new words are $0\le a<k<b\le5$,
$\binom{6}{3}=20$ of them, and

$|H_{2}^{*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$,

$N_{1}(i)=i(5-i)$, $N_{1}=20$, $N(n)=(n+1)(n^{2}-n+6)/6$, $N(5)=26$.
In that inclusive convention the unordered diploid count is $26\cdot27/2=351$, $26^{2}=676$ ordered.
This is the $26$ haplotype/$351$ genotype convention usually quoted.

The $2\sum_{k\le2}\binom42=22$ and $2^{5}-2=30$ figures are the phase-symmetric $t$-break counts. The $22$-haplotype count is the conventional $\le2$ break per lineage count, $11$ per phase, which excludes recombination of two first-generation recombinants. The $30$-string maximal set is obtained only if the reciprocal $1\to0$ phase is admitted on the same strand. Under the stated strand asymmetry and the strict obligatory internal crossover interpretation the biologically realised $+$ strand repertoire in $F_{3}$ is the $2^{n-2}=8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered genotype set, the $26/351$ numbers being the $k=0,5$-inclusive formalisation. Unresolved remains whether telomeric cuts are to be counted as a recombination event; with the problem statement “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ the strict $8/36$ count is the intended one, $26/351$ being the inclusive textbook book-keeping.
reflection_text.9:
The two inbred founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are P0=00000, P1=11111. Strand asymmetry is fixed to the 0→1 direction.

F1: P0/P1 is heterozygous. With an obligatory single internal crossover per gamete the F1 gametes – the chromosomes that enter the F2 – are the monotone thresholds
h_a = 0^a 1^{5-a}, 1≤a≤4,
i.e. 01111,00111,00011,00001. The two founders 00000,11111 are not produced by a genuine internal crossover. Up to the k=0,5 formal ends this is the 6-member set {0^t1^{5-t}:0≤t≤5}.

F2 → F3 : an F2 individual is h_a/h_b with a,b∈{1,2,3,4}. An orientation-fixed single crossover at k∈{1,2,3,4}
rec_k(h_a,h_b)[i]=h_a(i) i≤k, h_b(i) i>k
is always 0…1 on the + strand. Writing z=0 u2 u3 u4 1,
u_i is free. Indeed rec_k gives
0^{min(a,k)}1^{k-min(a,k)}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}
and for a<k<b it is 0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}. The three interior SNPs 2,3,4 are independent.

Hence with a genuine internal crossover in every meiosis the + strand gamete pool that can appear in F3 is
H3+ = {0 x2 x3 x4 1 : x_i∈{0,1}} = 2^{5-2}=2^3=8
haplotypes:
01111,00111,00011,00001,
01011,01001,01101,00101.
Four are the F1 monotone words, four are the first genuine two-meiosis
0^a1^b0^c1^d mosaics, e.g. 01011=0^11^10^11^2 etc. This is the 2^{n-2} obligatory-crossover core.

Unordered diploid F3 autosomes from these 8 haplotypes are
C(8+1,2)=36, 8^2=64 ordered.

Remark on conventions. If telomeric formal cuts k=0,5 are admitted as bookkeeping recombinants the F1 pool is enlarged to the six monotone words 0^t1^{5-t},0≤t≤5. Two successive orientation-fixed prefix–suffix replacements then give
rec_k(h_a,h_b)=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, m=min(a,k)
and the + strand words with at most one 1→0 descent
0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a≤k≤b≤5.
Number of distinct + strand haplotypes is
|H2|=(n+1)+C(n+1,3)=6+20=26,
20 genuinely new words of the form 0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} with 0≤a<k<b≤5, six monotone thresholds. This gives 26^2 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered diploid genotypes and is the 26-haplotype, 351-genotype inclusive count often quoted.

The textbook t-break per lineage count ∑_{k≤2}C(4,k)=11 per phase, 22 total phases, is the further restriction to at most two switches on a fixed parental background and does not allow recombination of two first-generation recombinants, which is exactly what occurs in F2→F3.

The unresolved point is the counting convention: strict “exactly one internal locus per gamete’’ → 8 + strand haplotypes, 36 unordered diploids; inclusive k=0,5 formal counting → 26 + strand haplotypes, 351 unordered diploids. The 22/30 numbers are the two-phase, ≤2-break/≤3-switch maximal combinatorial sets.
reflection_text.6:
The founder chromosomes on the chosen + strand can be written $0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$.
With orientation fixed a single orientation-fixed meiosis is the prefix–suffix
operation ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),i\le k$, $h_{b}(i),i>k$.
On the + strand the $F_{1}$ products of $0^{5}/1^{5}$ are the monotone
$0\to1$ thresholds $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$.

If the $k=0,5$ telomeric formal “no-crossover’’ ends are kept as book-keeping
recombinants $H_{1}^{+}=\{0^{a}1^{5-a}:0\le a\le5\}$, $|H_{1}^{+}|=6$.
Two successive orientation-fixed one-break meioses then give

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\;m=\min(a,k)$,

i.e. the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$.
$ a<k<b$ gives a genuine descent.  For a fixed descent position $i$
$N_{1}(i)=i(5-i)$ and

$N_{1}= \sum_{i=1}^{4}i(5-i)=20$,
$|H_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$,

$6$ monotone $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$ new $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
words.  In diploid terms $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed strand.
Removing the two parental haplotypes this is $20$ strictly new $F_{3}$
positive-strand haplotypes, $24$ new together with the parents.  The
$30=2\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{4}{i}$ count is the two-phase
$0\to1/1\to0$ maximal combinatorial set; the conventional two-break
per lineage $2\sum_{k\le2}\binom{4}{k}=22$ count is the $t$-break
$11$ per phase restriction.

The statement “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ is
the obligatory interior crossover convention $1\le k\le4$, $1\le a,b\le4$.
The $k=0,5$ formal ends are then discarded.  The $F_{1}$ pool on the + strand
is then $S_{1}=\{0^{a}1^{5-a}:1\le a\le4\}$, $|S_{1}|=4$, i.e. $01111,
00111,00011,00001$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is
$z=0u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}1$ with $u_{i}\in\{0,1\}$, the three interior SNPs being
free.  Hence the strictly interior one-crossover-per-meiosis + strand
repertoire in $F_{3}$ is

${\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}=\{0xxx1:x\in\{0,1\}^{3}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,
$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$,
four monotone $F_{1}$ words and the four genuinely new three-run words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.  Up to order this is $8^{2}=64$ ordered
and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes on the
chosen strand.  The $26$-haplotype $351$-genotype figure is the same
construction with the telomeric $k=0,5$ ends admitted; the $8$-haplotype
$36$-genotype figure is the physically strict obligatory-interior-crossover
realisation.  The discrepancy $26$ vs $8$, $351$ vs $36$, $22$ vs $30$
in the room is exactly this inclusive vs strict interior-crossover
book-keeping difference.

2.text:
On the fixed + strand write $0$ for the $P_{0}$ allele and $1$ for the $P_{1}$
allele.  With strand asymmetry the only first meiosis products which can
be seen on the chosen strand are the $0\to 1$ thresholds

$$
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le4,
$$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$, the two parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ being absent
because a crossover is obligatory in every gamete.  This is the $F_{1}$
gamete pool and hence the $F_{2}$ chromosome pool on the + strand,
$|S_{1}|=4$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the orientation fixed prefix–suffix

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\,i\le k,\qquad 
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\,i>k,
\qquad 1\le k\le4 ,
$$

$h_{a},h_{b}\in S_{1}$.  Put $z={\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$.  Then
$z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ and for $2\le i\le4$

$$
z_{i}=h_{a}(i)\;i\le k,\qquad z_{i}=h_{b}(i)\;i>k,
$$

so the three interior sites are free and $z$ is always of the form
$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.  Explicitly

$$
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
       =\{01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101\},
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosome
sequences.  The four monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes and the four
words

$$
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,
$$

are the first genuine two-meiosis recombinants $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$1\le a<k<b\le4$.  In particular the three interior SNPs are free in
$F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the arbitrarily chosen
positive strand.

Up to order the eight $+$–strand haplotypes can be paired in an $F_{3}$
diploid.  Ordered maternal/paternal pairs are $8^{2}=64$ and unordered
diploid autosomes are

$$
N_{g}=\binom{H+1}{2}=\frac{8\cdot9}{2}=36,
$$

the $8$ haplotypes above being the distinct chromosome sequences which
can be present in $F_{3}$ on the fixed strand.  The four $F_{1}$ haplotypes
are contained in the set as the monotone cases $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$.

Remark.  If the degenerate telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept as formal
recombinations the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the orientation-fixed two-step set is
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$.  The + strand
haplotype pool is then

$$
|H_{2}^{{\rm inc}}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,
$$

$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes, the $20$ words with $0\le a<k<b\le5$ being the usual
inclusive $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count.  The $8=2^{\,n-2}$ set above is
the strict obligatory-interior-crossover, $k=1\ldots4$, realisation of
that construction. ∎

1.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the two inbred founders can be written
$P_{0}=0^{5}=00000$, $P_{1}=1^{5}=11111$ and with the stated strand
asymmetry a meiosis can only make the $0\to 1$ orientation.  With the
conventional notation

$$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 0\le a\le5, $$

a single orientation–fixed one break is

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]\,h_{b}[k+1:5]$ .

With an obligatory interior break the $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the $+$
strand is

${\cal S}_{1}= \{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}= \{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ ,

$|{\cal S}_{1}|=4$, the two formal ends $k=0,5$ being the no crossover
limits.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ with
$1\le k\le4$.  Then

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}
$

and in particular $z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ for every product.  Writing
$z=0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1$,

$z_{i}=h_{a}(i)$ for $i\le k$ and $z_{i}=h_{b}(i)$ for $i>k$, so that the
three interior sites $2,3,4$ can be chosen independently.  Hence on the
fixed $0\to1$ phase

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= \{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$$

i.e. the $2^{\,n-2}$ $0\ldots1$ words.  For $n=5$

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= 
01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosomes.  The four
monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes, the four
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ are the first genuine two–meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ recombinants.  The three interior SNPs are free in
$F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the chosen strand.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random.  There
are $H^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{g}= \binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand.  This is
the $2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory–internal–crossover realisation.

Remark.  If the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept in the
book-keeping the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone thresholds
$0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation–fixed
prefix–suffix replacements then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one
$1\to0$ descent

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$–strand
haplotypes, $6$ monotone $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$
genuinely new two-break mosaics.  Ordered diploid $26^{2}=676$, unordered
$26\cdot27/2=351$, the usual $ (n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ inclusive count.  The
$8$–haplotype $36$–genotype set above is the strict $k=1\ldots4$
obligatory–crossover version of this construction. ∎

8.text:
On the $+$ strand put the two founders $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and
write an orientation fixed one crossover product as the prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad 
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k$,

on the $+$ strand.  With the asymmetry stated a meiosis can only make the
$0\to1$ phase.  An obligatory internal crossover is $1\le k\le4$ and an
$F_{1}$ gamete is therefore the obligatory monotone mosaic

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le4$,

$S_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$, $|S_{1}^{+}|=4$, the two
formal telomeric products $0^{5},1^{5}$ being discarded by the
‘exactly one internal locus per gamete’ convention.

Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\,h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}\in S_{1}^{+}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ break be $k\in\{1,2,
3,4\}$.  Then

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{i}=0\iff i\le\min(a,k)\ {\rm or}\ k<i\le b$,

so every $F_{3}$ gamete is $0\ldots1$ on the $+$ strand and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$ .

For $a<k<b$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,

and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Hence

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}=2^{\,5-2}$,

i.e.

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,
$01011,01001,01101,00101$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosomes.  The four
monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes, the four words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ are the first genuine two-meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ mosaics.  In particular the three interior SNPs
are free in $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the
fixed $+$ strand.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired arbitrarily.  Up to
maternal/paternal order

$N_{g}^{\rm ord}=H^{2}=64$,

and unordered

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=8\cdot9/2=36$

distinct $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the chosen strand.  This is the
$2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory-internal-crossover bound.

Remark.  If the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept as textbook
book-keeping the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone
$0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation-fixed
prefix–suffix replacements then give

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad
0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $0\to1$ haplotypes
on the fixed strand, $20$ of them with the form $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}
1^{5-b},\,0\le a<k<b\le5$, i.e. $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes.  The $8$–haplotype,
$36$–genotype set above is the $k=1\ldots4$ strictly internal realisation
of this inclusive count. ∎

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $0$ for the $A$ allele and $1$ for the
$B$ allele

$P_{0}=00000$ , $P_{1}=11111$.

With strand asymmetry fixed a meiosis is the orientation fixed
prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(x,y)=x[1:k]\,y[k+1:5],\qquad 1\le k\le 4,$

i.e. a genuine obligatory internal crossover.  On $P_{0}/P_{1}$ this
gives the $0\to 1$ monotone mosaics

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad1\le a\le 4$,

$H_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad |H_{1}^{+}|=4$,

the two founders $00000,11111$ never being made by a genuine
crossover.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i]\;i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}[i]\;i>k$ .

Hence ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and ends
with $1$ and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$.

It is monotone iff $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ and it is genuinely two–
break iff $a<k<b$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},
\qquad1\le a<k<b\le4.$

The three interior sites $2,3,4$ are therefore free.  Writing
$z=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ every $x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ is realised, e.g.

$k=1:\;01111,00111,00011,00001$,
$k=2:\;01111,01011,01001,00111,00011,00001$,
$k=3:\;01111,01101,00111,00101,00011,00001$,
$k=4:\;01111,00111,00011,00001$,

so that on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
   =\{01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101\}$, 

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct positive-strand
haplotypes.  Four are the $F_{1}$ monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words and

$01011,01001,01101,00101$

are the four $\binom43=4$ genuinely new $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ two–
meiosis mosaics first seen in $F_{3}$.  No $1\ldots0$ word can ever be
seen on the chosen strand because of the stated strand asymmetry.

In diploid terms the eight haplotypes can be paired at random in an
$F_{3}$ zygote.  There are $8^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs
and

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}= \binom{H+1}{2}= \frac{8\cdot9}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the positive strand, i.e. $36$
different diploid sequences, $8$ distinct haploid sequences.

Remark.  If the degenerate telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept as formal
recombinants the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone words
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation-fixed
prefix-suffix meioses then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one
$1\to0$ descent

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

$|H_{2}^{*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ positive-strand
haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the usual $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ inclusive
text-book count.  The $8$-haplotype, $36$-genotype set above is the
obligatory internal-crossover, $k=1\ldots4$, realisation of that set
under the literal “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’
reading. ∎

4.text:
On the strand which is kept the two founders can be written
$P_{0}=0^{5},\,P_{1}=1^{5}$ on the $+$ strand.  With the strand
asymmetry a single orientation fixed meiosis in $P_{0}/P_{1}$ can only
make the monotone $0\to 1$ mosaics

$$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}\qquad 0\le t\le5 .$$

With an obligatory internal break the $k=0,5$ non–recombinants are
not made and on the $+$ strand

$${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{h_{a}:1\le a\le4\}
      =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad|{\cal H}_{1}^{+}|=4, $$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$,
$a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete on the fixed
orientation is the prefix–suffix product

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k,
\qquad1\le k\le4,$$

so that on the $+$ strand

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}
0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}.$$

In particular ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and
ends with $1$ and for $a<k<b$

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, $$

i.e. the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Hence on the fixed
$0\to1$ phase

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\},$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct positive–strand
chromosomes, viz.

$$\begin{array}{llll}
01111,&00111,&00011,&00001,\\
01011,&01001,&01101,&00101,
\end{array}$$

the four monotone $F_{1}$ words $01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the four
genuinely new two–meiosis words $01011,01001,01101,00101$.  The three
interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be
seen on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand.  In diploid terms the
$H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random, $H^{2}=64$ ordered and

$$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=\frac{8\times9}{2}=36$$

unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the chosen strand.

Remark.  With the usual textbook book–keeping the formal telomeric
cuts $k=0,5$ are kept.  The $F_{1}$ pool is then the six monotone
thresholds $0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$ and the orientation-fixed
two-step prefix–suffix set is

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

i.e. the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  This is

$$|H_{2}^{+,*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,\qquad n=5,$$

$6$ monotone $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$ new
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<k<b\le5$, words on the $+$
strand, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes, the $8=2^{\,n-2}$ words above being the
obligatory-internal-crossover $k=1\ldots4$, $a,b=1\ldots4$ realisation
of the set.  This is the conventional $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ 
$26$-haplotype, $351$-genotype count. ∎

9.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+ $ strand write the two homozygous founders
as $P_{0}=0^{5},P_{1}=1^{5}$ and put the $0\to1$ threshold

$$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}\qquad 1\le a\le 4\; ,$$

for the $F_{1}$ gamete which is obtained from $P_{0}/P_{1}$ by one
obligatory internal cross-over.  With the strand asymmetry fixed the
$F_{1}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand is therefore

$$S_{1}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad|S_{1}|=4, $$

the two formal ends $k=0,5$ being excluded by the “exactly one internal
locus per gamete’’ requirement.

An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the orientation fixed prefix–suffix

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k,
\qquad 1\le k\le 4.$$

Hence ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and ends with
$1$.  Writing $z=0u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}1$,

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}
1^{5-b},$$

so that for $a<k<b$

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, $$

and $u_{2},u_{3},u_{4}$ can be chosen independently.  In fact

* $k=1$ gives the four monotone $F_{1}$ words,
* $k=2$ gives $0\,h_{a}[2]\,h_{b}[3]\,h_{b}[4]\,1$,
* $k=3$ gives $0\,h_{a}[2]\,h_{a}[3]\,h_{b}[4]\,1$,
* $k=4$ gives $0\,h_{a}[2]\,h_{a}[3]\,h_{a}[4]\,1$,

so that on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8 $$

distinct $+$–strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete and
hence by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,

$$01111,00111,00011,00001,
\;01011,01001,01101,00101,$$

the first four being the $F_{1}$ monotone words and
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ being the first genuine two–meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ recombinants.  The three interior SNPs $2,3,4$
are free in $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the
chosen strand.

Up to order the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired in an $F_{3}$ zygote.
Ordered maternal/paternal pairs are $H^{2}=64$ and

$$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=\frac{8\times 9}{2}=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the $+$ strand.  This is the
$2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory-internal-crossover core.

Remark.  If the telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ are admitted as
book-keeping recombinants the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six
monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t},0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation
fixed prefix–suffix replacements then give the $0\to1$ words with at
most one $1\to0$ descent

$$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a\le k\le b\le5, $$

$|H_{2}^{\rm inc}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand
haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes, the $20$ words $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$0\le a<k<b\le5$, being the usual inclusive two-generation
one-crossover bound.  Discarding the formal $k=0,5$ ends this reduces
to the $8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered diploid, strict internal
crossover set quoted above. ∎

5.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write $0$ for the $A$–parental allele
and $1$ for the $B$–parental allele

$P_{0}=0^{5}, \qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$ .

With the stated strand asymmetry a single orientation fixed meiosis can
only make the monotone $0\to1$ thresholds

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}, \qquad 1\le t\le 4,$

on the $+$ strand.  In particular the obligatory internal crossover in
the $P_{0}/P_{1}$ $F_{1}$ makes

$S_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad |S_{1}^{+}|=4,$

the two formal telomeric products $0^{5},1^{5}$ being the $k=0,5$
non-recombinants.  The $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis on the $+$ strand is the orientation fixed
prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\,i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\,i>k,\qquad 1\le k\le4,$

so that

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}
0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$ .

Hence ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and ends with
$1$ and for $a<k<b$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$.

The three interior markers $2,3,4$ are therefore free.  Up to the fixed
$0\to1$ phase

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{\,0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$,

i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosomes

$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\;
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$,

the four monotone $F_{1}$ words and the four first genuine two-meiosis
mosaics $01011,01001,01101,00101$.  In particular the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool on the chosen strand is the $0\ldots1$ family $2^{\,n-2}$.

Pairing the eight haplotypes at random gives $H^{2}=64$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=8\cdot9/2=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation.
The four $F_{1}$ haplotypes are the special cases $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$.
This is the obligatory internal $k=1\ldots4$ realisation.

Remark.  With the usual textbook book-keeping the formal telomeric
cuts $k=0,5$ are kept, $H_{1}^{+}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}$,
$|H_{1}^{+}|=6$.  Two successive orientation-fixed single cuts then give
the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$.  The number of
distinct $+$–strand haplotypes is then

$|H_{2}^{*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$,

$20=\binom63$ genuinely new $F_{3}$ mosaics, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed
strand.  Removing the $k=0,5$ formal non-recombinants recovers the
strict $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered genotype, set above. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the arbitrarily chosen positive strand fixed the two founders are $P_{0}=00000$, $P_{1}=11111$ and strand
asymmetry is taken to allow recombination in only the $0\to1$ orientation on that strand.

First meiosis $P_{0}/P_{1}\to F_{1}$. On the $+$ strand a single
orientation-fixed crossover is a prefix–suffix,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i],\,i\le k,\;h_{b}[i],\,i>k$,

so every $F_{1}$ gamete that can be seen on the $+$ strand is a monotone
threshold

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le5$,

$|H_{1}|=n+1=6$.  Up to the formal $k=0,5$ telomeric ends this is the whole
$F_{1}$ gamete pool on the chosen strand.  The $F_{2}$ is therefore
$h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a},h_{b}\in H_{1}$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is again an orientation-fixed prefix–suffix
of two $H_{1}$ haplotypes.  With $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $m=\min(a,k)$,

hence on the $+$ strand a second-generation gamete is always $0\ldots1$
and can have at most one $1\to0$ descent.  Up to the $k=0,5$ ends the
non-trivial words are

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<k<b\le5,$

i.e. a word with an initial $0$-run of length $a$, a first $1$-run ending
at $k$ and a second $0$ -run ending at $b$. The triple $(a,k,b)$ is
uniquely recovered from the word.

The six monotone thresholds are recovered for $a\ge k$ or $k\ge b$.
The genuinely new $F_{3}$ mosaics are $0\le a<k<b\le5$. The number of
triples is

$\#\{0\le a<k<b\le5\}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

$N_{1}(k)=k(5-k)$ words with the descent at $k$, $\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=20$.

Hence on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation

$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different positive-strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete
and therefore by an $F_{3}$ chromosome: the $6$ monotone
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and the $20$ one-descent words
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$,

e.g. $11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$ and
$10111,10011,\dots,00101,00010$ etc.  In diploid terms this is
$H_{2}^{2}=676$ ordered and $H_{2}(H_{2}+1)/2=26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand.

The $2\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{4}{i}=30=2^{5}-2$ set is the maximal
combinatorial set obtained if the reciprocal $1\to0$ phase is counted as
distinct on the same strand, i.e. if the two monotone orientations
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and $1^{t}0^{5-t}$ are both admitted as first-meiosis
products.  With the stated strand asymmetry recombination is realised in
only one orientation on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand, so the
$1\to0$ first-meiosis phase is not realisable on that strand and the 30
words are a phase double count of the $26$ $0\to1$ words above.  The
conventional $2\sum_{k\le2}\binom{4}{k}=22$ per-lineage count excludes
recombination of two first-generation recombinants and is therefore a
strict subset of the two-meiosis prefix–suffix set.

Discarding the formal $k=0,5$ telomeric ends the obligatory internal
crossover core is the $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ words $0xxx1$, i.e. the four
monotone $F_{1}$ words $01111,00111,00011,00001$ together with
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes,
which is the $k=1\ldots4$ interior-crossover version of the same
$26$-haplotype inclusive count. ∎

6.text:
On the chosen $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}=00000$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}=11111$

and fix the orientation of the single one-break meiosis to be

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i]\;i\le k$, 
${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}[i]\;i>k$ , 
$1\le k\le 4 $,

the $k=0,5$ telomeric ``no crossover'' limits being discarded by the
obligatory interior-crossover hypothesis.  On the $+$ strand an
$A/B$ heterozygote can therefore only make the $0\to1$ thresholds

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ .

With an obligatory $1\le k\le4$ break the $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the
$+$ strand is

$S_{1}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}
      =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad |S_{1}|=4 ,$

the two formal founders $0^{5},1^{5}$ being $k=0,5$ limits.  An $F_{2}$
plant is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a},h_{b}\in S_{1}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ with $1\le k\le4$.
Writing $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
$

so that every $F_{3}$ gamete is $0\ldots1$ on the fixed strand and
$z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$.  For $a<k<b$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},$

and for $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ the product is again a monotone
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  In particular the three interior markers $2,3,4$ are
free.  Writing $z=0\,u_{2}u_{3}u_{4}\,1$,

$\;{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}=\{\,0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}\;
      =\{0xxx1\}$

on the arbitrarily chosen orientation.  Hence

$|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8 $

distinct $+$–strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete and
hence by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,

$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,$
$01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,$

the first four being the $F_{1}$ monotone gametes and

$01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$

the four genuinely new $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ three-run mosaics first
seen in $F_{3}$.  The three interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$ and no
$1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the fixed $+$ strand.

In diploid terms the eight $+$–strand haplotypes can be paired
arbitrarily.  Up to order there are

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes, $H^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal
pairs, on the chosen strand.  The four monotone words are the $F_{1}$
gametes, the four $01011,01001,01101,00101$ words being the first
two-meiosis recombinants.

Remark.  Keeping the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ as book keeping
recombinants the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone thresholds
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the orientation fixed two-step
prefix–suffix set is

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

i.e. $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The inclusive
$+$–strand count is then

$|H_{2}^{+ *}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$,

$6$ monotone $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$ new $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
words, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ genotypes on the fixed strand, the $20$ words
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\,0\le a<k<b\le5$, being the conventionally
quoted $F_{3}$ recombinants.  Discarding the $k=0,5$ formal ends this
is the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered diploid, obligatory
interior-crossover realisation quoted above. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the two inbred founders are
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$.  With the stated strand asymmetry a
single meiosis can only make the $0\to1$ threshold

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le5,$

on the + strand.  The $F_{1}$ zygote is $P_{0}/P_{1}$ so the $F_{2}$
chromosomes are exactly the $H_{1}$ thresholds.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
meiosis is the orientation fixed prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k$

$0\le k\le5$, $h_{a},h_{b}\in H_{1}$.  With $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ and $m=\min(a,k)$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{\,k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$ ,

i.e. up to the trivial $k=0,5$ ends

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

a + strand word with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The triple
$(a,k,b)$ is uniquely recoverable from the word: $a$ is the length of
the initial $0$–run, $k$ is the end of the first $1$–run and $b$ is the
end of the second $0$–run.  Hence distinct triples give distinct
+ strand haplotypes.

The six monotone thresholds $0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, are the
$a\ge k$ or $k\ge b$ cases.  The genuinely new $F_{3}$ mosaics are
$0\le a<k<b\le5$.  Their number is

$N_{1}=\#\{0\le a<k<b\le5\}=\binom{6}{3}=20,$

and

$N_{1}(k)=k(5-k)$ per break,

$\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$.

Hence on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation the + strand haplotype pool
that can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete and therefore by an $F_{3}$
chromosome is

$|H_{2}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}
       =6+20=26$

distinct $0\to1$ strings, $6$ $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20$ two-meiosis
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ words with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.  For $n=5$

$N(n)=\dfrac{(n+1)(n^{2}-n+6)}6$, $N(5)=26$,

$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes on the chosen strand.

This is the conventional $k=0,5$ inclusive count.  The $2^{\,n-2}=8$
$0xxx1$ set is the physically strict obligatory-internal-crossover
core obtained by discarding the formal telomeric $k=0,5$ ends,
$|H_{1}^{i}|=4$ and $H_{2}^{i}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}$.

The $30$ figure $2\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{4}{i}$ is the maximal
combinatorial set obtained only if the reciprocal $1\to0$ phase is
counted as a distinct first-meiosis product on the same strand.  With
the stated sufficient asymmetry of the strands recombination is
realised in only one orientation on the arbitrarily chosen + strand,
so the $1\to0$ mirror half of the $30$ set is not realised on that
strand.  $30$ is therefore a double count of phase on the + strand;
the attainable + strand repertoire under the stated orientation
restriction is the $26$ $0\to1$ haplotypes above, and the $8$
$0xxx1$ obligatory-internal-crossover core is the $k=1\ldots4$ limit of
the same construction. ∎

public_text.2:
On the fixed + strand write $0$ for the $P_{0}$ allele and $1$ for the $P_{1}$
allele.  With strand asymmetry the only first meiosis products which can
be seen on the chosen strand are the $0\to 1$ thresholds

$$
h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le4,
$$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$, the two parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ being absent
because a crossover is obligatory in every gamete.  This is the $F_{1}$
gamete pool and hence the $F_{2}$ chromosome pool on the + strand,
$|S_{1}|=4$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the orientation fixed prefix–suffix

$$
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\,i\le k,\qquad 
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\,i>k,
\qquad 1\le k\le4 ,
$$

$h_{a},h_{b}\in S_{1}$.  Put $z={\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$.  Then
$z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ and for $2\le i\le4$

$$
z_{i}=h_{a}(i)\;i\le k,\qquad z_{i}=h_{b}(i)\;i>k,
$$

so the three interior sites are free and $z$ is always of the form
$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.  Explicitly

$$
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
       =\{01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101\},
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosome
sequences.  The four monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes and the four
words

$$
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,
$$

are the first genuine two-meiosis recombinants $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$1\le a<k<b\le4$.  In particular the three interior SNPs are free in
$F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the arbitrarily chosen
positive strand.

Up to order the eight $+$–strand haplotypes can be paired in an $F_{3}$
diploid.  Ordered maternal/paternal pairs are $8^{2}=64$ and unordered
diploid autosomes are

$$
N_{g}=\binom{H+1}{2}=\frac{8\cdot9}{2}=36,
$$

the $8$ haplotypes above being the distinct chromosome sequences which
can be present in $F_{3}$ on the fixed strand.  The four $F_{1}$ haplotypes
are contained in the set as the monotone cases $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$.

Remark.  If the degenerate telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept as formal
recombinations the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the orientation-fixed two-step set is
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$.  The + strand
haplotype pool is then

$$
|H_{2}^{{\rm inc}}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,
$$

$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes, the $20$ words with $0\le a<k<b\le5$ being the usual
inclusive $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count.  The $8=2^{\,n-2}$ set above is
the strict obligatory-interior-crossover, $k=1\ldots4$, realisation of
that construction. ∎
public_text.1:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the two inbred founders can be written
$P_{0}=0^{5}=00000$, $P_{1}=1^{5}=11111$ and with the stated strand
asymmetry a meiosis can only make the $0\to 1$ orientation.  With the
conventional notation

$$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 0\le a\le5, $$

a single orientation–fixed one break is

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]\,h_{b}[k+1:5]$ .

With an obligatory interior break the $F_{1}$ gamete pool on the $+$
strand is

${\cal S}_{1}= \{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}= \{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ ,

$|{\cal S}_{1}|=4$, the two formal ends $k=0,5$ being the no crossover
limits.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ with
$1\le k\le4$.  Then

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}
$

and in particular $z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ for every product.  Writing
$z=0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1$,

$z_{i}=h_{a}(i)$ for $i\le k$ and $z_{i}=h_{b}(i)$ for $i>k$, so that the
three interior sites $2,3,4$ can be chosen independently.  Hence on the
fixed $0\to1$ phase

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= \{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$$

i.e. the $2^{\,n-2}$ $0\ldots1$ words.  For $n=5$

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= 
01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,
01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosomes.  The four
monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes, the four
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ are the first genuine two–meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ recombinants.  The three interior SNPs are free in
$F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the chosen strand.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random.  There
are $H^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{g}= \binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand.  This is
the $2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory–internal–crossover realisation.

Remark.  If the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept in the
book-keeping the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone thresholds
$0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation–fixed
prefix–suffix replacements then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one
$1\to0$ descent

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$–strand
haplotypes, $6$ monotone $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$
genuinely new two-break mosaics.  Ordered diploid $26^{2}=676$, unordered
$26\cdot27/2=351$, the usual $ (n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ inclusive count.  The
$8$–haplotype $36$–genotype set above is the strict $k=1\ldots4$

public_text.8:
On the $+$ strand put the two founders $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and
write an orientation fixed one crossover product as the prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad 
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k$,

on the $+$ strand.  With the asymmetry stated a meiosis can only make the
$0\to1$ phase.  An obligatory internal crossover is $1\le k\le4$ and an
$F_{1}$ gamete is therefore the obligatory monotone mosaic

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le4$,

$S_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$, $|S_{1}^{+}|=4$, the two
formal telomeric products $0^{5},1^{5}$ being discarded by the
‘exactly one internal locus per gamete’ convention.

Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\,h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}\in S_{1}^{+}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ break be $k\in\{1,2,
3,4\}$.  Then

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{i}=0\iff i\le\min(a,k)\ {\rm or}\ k<i\le b$,

so every $F_{3}$ gamete is $0\ldots1$ on the $+$ strand and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$ .

For $a<k<b$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,

and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Hence

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}=2^{\,5-2}$,

i.e.

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,
$01011,01001,01101,00101$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand chromosomes.  The four
monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes, the four words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ are the first genuine two-meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ mosaics.  In particular the three interior SNPs
are free in $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the
fixed $+$ strand.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired arbitrarily.  Up to
maternal/paternal order

$N_{g}^{\rm ord}=H^{2}=64$,

and unordered

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=8\cdot9/2=36$

distinct $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the chosen strand.  This is the
$2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory-internal-crossover bound.

Remark.  If the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept as textbook
book-keeping the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone
$0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation-fixed
prefix–suffix replacements then give

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad
0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $0\to1$ haplotypes
on the fixed strand, $20$ of them with the form $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}
1^{5-b},\,0\le a<k<b\le5$, i.e. $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes.  The $8$–haplotype,
$36$–genotype set above is the $k=1\ldots4$ strictly internal realisation
of this inclusive count. ∎
public_text.3:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $0$ for the $A$ allele and $1$ for the
$B$ allele

$P_{0}=00000$ , $P_{1}=11111$.

With strand asymmetry fixed a meiosis is the orientation fixed
prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(x,y)=x[1:k]\,y[k+1:5],\qquad 1\le k\le 4,$

i.e. a genuine obligatory internal crossover.  On $P_{0}/P_{1}$ this
gives the $0\to 1$ monotone mosaics

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad1\le a\le 4$,

$H_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad |H_{1}^{+}|=4$,

the two founders $00000,11111$ never being made by a genuine
crossover.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i]\;i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}[i]\;i>k$ .

Hence ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and ends
with $1$ and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$.

It is monotone iff $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ and it is genuinely two–
break iff $a<k<b$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},
\qquad1\le a<k<b\le4.$

The three interior sites $2,3,4$ are therefore free.  Writing
$z=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ every $x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ is realised, e.g.

$k=1:\;01111,00111,00011,00001$,
$k=2:\;01111,01011,01001,00111,00011,00001$,
$k=3:\;01111,01101,00111,00101,00011,00001$,
$k=4:\;01111,00111,00011,00001$,

so that on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
   =\{01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101\}$, 

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct positive-strand
haplotypes.  Four are the $F_{1}$ monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words and

$01011,01001,01101,00101$

are the four $\binom43=4$ genuinely new $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ two–
meiosis mosaics first seen in $F_{3}$.  No $1\ldots0$ word can ever be
seen on the chosen strand because of the stated strand asymmetry.

In diploid terms the eight haplotypes can be paired at random in an
$F_{3}$ zygote.  There are $8^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs
and

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}= \binom{H+1}{2}= \frac{8\cdot9}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the positive strand, i.e. $36$
different diploid sequences, $8$ distinct haploid sequences.

Remark.  If the degenerate telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are kept as formal
recombinants the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone words
$0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$.  Two successive orientation-fixed
prefix-suffix meioses then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one
$1\to0$ descent

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

$|H_{2}^{*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ positive-strand
haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the usual $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ inclusive
text-book count.  The $8$-haplotype, $36$-genotype set above is the
obligatory internal-crossover, $k=1\ldots4$, realisation of that set
under the literal “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’
reading. ∎
public_text.4:
On the strand which is kept the two founders can be written
$P_{0}=0^{5},\,P_{1}=1^{5}$ on the $+$ strand.  With the strand
asymmetry a single orientation fixed meiosis in $P_{0}/P_{1}$ can only
make the monotone $0\to 1$ mosaics

$$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}\qquad 0\le t\le5 .$$

With an obligatory internal break the $k=0,5$ non–recombinants are
not made and on the $+$ strand

$${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{h_{a}:1\le a\le4\}
      =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\qquad|{\cal H}_{1}^{+}|=4, $$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$,
$a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete on the fixed
orientation is the prefix–suffix product

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k,
\qquad1\le k\le4,$$

so that on the $+$ strand

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}
0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}.$$

In particular ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$ always starts with $0$ and
ends with $1$ and for $a<k<b$

$${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, $$

i.e. the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Hence on the fixed

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\},$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct positive–strand
chromosomes, viz.

$$\begin{array}{llll}
01111,&00111,&00011,&00001,\\
01011,&01001,&01101,&00101,
\end{array}$$

the four monotone $F_{1}$ words $01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the four
genuinely new two–meiosis words $01011,01001,01101,00101$.  The three
interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be

$H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random, $H^{2}=64$ ordered and

$$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=\frac{8\times9}{2}=36$$

unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the chosen strand.

Remark.  With the usual textbook book–keeping the formal telomeric
cuts $k=0,5$ are kept.  The $F_{1}$ pool is then the six monotone
thresholds $0^{t}1^{5-t},\,0\le t\le5$ and the orientation-fixed
two-step prefix–suffix set is

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

i.e. the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  This is

$$|H_{2}^{+,*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,\qquad n=5,$$

$6$ monotone $F_{1}$ thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$ new
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<k<b\le5$, words on the $+$
strand, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes, the $8=2^{\,n-2}$ words above being the
obligatory-internal-crossover $k=1\ldots4$, $a,b=1\ldots4$ realisation
of the set.  This is the conventional $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ 
$26$-haplotype, $351$-genotype count. ∎

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $m=\min(a,k)$,

2.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$.
With the stated strand asymmetry a one-break meiosis is the
orientation fixed prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\,i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\,i>k$,

and with an obligatory interior break $1\le k\le 4$.
On $P_{0}/P_{1}$ this gives the $0\to1$ thresholds

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad1\le t\le4$,

${\cal S}_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$, $|{\cal S}_{1}^{+}|=4$,
the $k=0,5$ telomeric limits being excluded by the obligatory
internal crossover.

An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is ${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})$,
$1\le k\le4$.  With $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}
0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$,

so that $z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ for every product and, for $a<k<b$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$.

Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$–strand gamete is of the form
$z=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.
On the fixed $0\to1$ phase

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$

is attainable and no $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the chosen
strand.  For $n=5$

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=01111,00111,00011,00001,
01011,01001,01101,00101$,

i.e. $|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand
haplotypes.  The four monotone words are the $F_{1}$ gametes and
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ are the first genuine two-meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ recombinants.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random.
Ordered maternal/paternal pairs are $H^{2}=64$ and up to order

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=8\cdot9/2=36$

different diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand,
the $36$ unordered genotypes being the $8$ haplotypes above in
pairing.  This is the strict $k=1\ldots4$ obligatory-internal-crossover
core.  With the usual textbook $k=0,5$ formal telomeric book-keeping
the $+$–strand inclusive pool is
$|H^{*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ haplotypes,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ genotypes, of which the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0xxx1$ set is the
obligatory interior-crossover realisation. ∎

6.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand let $0$ be the allele of the first inbred
and $1$ the allele of the second inbred

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$ .

With the stated strand asymmetry a meiosis on the chosen strand is the
orientation fixed prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\qquad 
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k$
with the obligatory interior break $1\le k\le4$.

On $P_{0}/P_{1}$ this is the $0\to1$ monotone threshold

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad1\le a\le4$,

$H_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\},\;|H_{1}^{+}|=4$,

the $k=0,5$ telomeric non-recombinants being excluded by the
‘exactly one interior locus per gamete’ requirement.

An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}
1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4,$

so that every $F_{3}$ gamete on the fixed strand satisfies
$z_{1}=0,\;z_{5}=1$ and

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ for $a<k<b$.
In particular

$z=0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1,\qquad x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$,

and the three interior SNPs $2,3,4$ are free in $F_{3}$.  No
$1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the chosen strand.

Hence on the $0\to1$ phase

${\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$
distinct + strand chromosomes

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,
$01011,01001,01101,00101$,

the first four being the $F_{1}$ monotone gametes and
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ the first genuine two-meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ mosaics.  This is the $k=1\ldots4$ obligatory
internal-crossover core.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ + strand haplotypes can be paired at random,
$H^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=8\cdot9/2=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand.  Keeping
the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ as book-keeping recombinants the
inclusive $0\to1$ count is $|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$
haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid genotypes, of which the $8=2^{n-2}$ $0xxx1$ set above is the
strict $k=1\ldots4$ realisation. ∎

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $0$ for the $P_{0}$ allele and $1$
for the $P_{1}$ allele

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$ ,

and fix the orientation of the one break meiosis to be the prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(x,y)[i]=x[i],\;i\le k,\qquad {\rm rec}_{k}(x,y)[i]=y[i],\;i>k$,

$1\le k\le4$,  the obligatory internal crossover.  With strand
asymmetry the only products which can be seen on the $+$ strand are the
$0\to1$ phase.

$P_{0}/P_{1}\to F_{1}$ gives on the $+$ strand the obligatory monotone
thresholds

$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\qquad 1\le a\le4,$

${\cal S}_{1}^{+}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ , $|{\cal S}_{1}^{+}|=4$,
the two formal telomeric $0^{5},1^{5}$ products being the $k=0,5$ limits
and being excluded by the “exactly one internal locus per gamete’’
requirement.  An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$, $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.

For an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$,
$1\le k\le4$,

so that every $F_{3}$ gamete on the fixed strand starts with $0$ and ends
with $1$.  Writing $z=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ we have $z_{i}=h_{a}(i)$ for
$i\le k$ and $z_{i}=h_{b}(i)$ for $i>k$ and therefore the three interior
sites $2,3,4$ are free.  For $a<k<b$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,

and for $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ the product is again monotone.

Hence on the fixed $0\to1$ phase

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
= \{0xxx1\}$

and

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$

distinct $+$–strand chromosomes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete and
hence by an $F_{3}$ chromosome.  Explicitly

$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,$
$01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101,$

the four monotone $F_{1}$ words and the four first genuine
two–meiosis $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ mosaics $01011,01001,01101,00101$.
No $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the chosen strand because of the
stated strand asymmetry and the three interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ haplotypes can be paired at random.  Ordered
maternal/paternal pairs are $H^{2}=64$ and unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand are

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$,

$64$ ordered, the usual $2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory–internal–crossover core.

Remark.  Keeping the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ as textbook
book–keeping, $H_{1}^{+*}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}$, $|H_{1}^{+*}|=6$,
two successive orientation-fixed prefix–suffix replacements give

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The inclusive
$+$–strand count is then

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$,

$6$ monotone thresholds and $20=\binom{6}{3}$ one-descent words,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes on the fixed strand.  The $8=2^{\,n-2}$ haplotype, $36$
unordered genotype set above is the $k=1\ldots4$ strictly internal
crossover realisation of this inclusive construction, i.e. the literal
“exactly one internal locus per generation for every gamete’’ reading. ∎

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write $0$ for the $P_{0}$ allele and
$1$ for the $P_{1}$ allele,

$P_{0}=0^{5}=00000$, $\;P_{1}=1^{5}=11111$,

the four monotone $F_{1}$ words and the four first genuine

No $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on the chosen strand.

Pairing the $H=8$ $+$–strand haplotypes at random in an $F_{3}$ zygote
gives $H^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and up to order

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$

distinct unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand,
the $2^{\,n-2}$ obligatory-internal-crossover core.

Remark.  Keeping the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ as book-keeping

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $0\to1$
$+$–strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the usual inclusive
$(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count.  The $8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered
genotype set above is the strict $k=1\ldots4$, $a,b=1\ldots4$
obligatory internal-crossover realisation of that construction. ∎

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$ .

swap

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}= \binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$

the usual inclusive $(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count.

Remark.  With the formal telomeric book-keeping $k=0,5$ the $F_{1}$ pool
is enlarged to $h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, $|H_{1}|=6$.  Two
successive orientation-fixed prefix–suffix replacements then give the
$0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$, i.e.

$|H_{2}^{*,+}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

$+$ strand haplotypes, $20=\binom63$ genuinely new $0\le a<k<b\le5$
words, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes.  Removing the formal $k=0,5$ ends recovers the strict
$2^{\,n-2}=8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered diploid, core above. ∎

1.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $0$ for the $P_{0}$ allele and
$1$ for the $P_{1}$ allele

$P_{0}=0^{5}=00000 ,\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}=11111 $

and fix the orientation fixed one break to the $0\to 1$ phase on that
strand.  With an obligatory interior break $1\le k\le4$ an $A/B$
heterozygote can only make a monotone threshold

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ .

In $P_{0}/P_{1}$ the obligatory $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ meiosis therefore gives
on the $+$ strand

${\cal S}_{1}^{+}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:1\le t\le4\}
          =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ , $|{\cal S}_{1}^{+}|=4$,

the two formal $k=0,5$ ends $00000,11111$ being excluded by the
‘exactly one interior locus per gamete’ requirement.  An $F_{2}$ is
$h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete on
the fixed $0\to1$ orientation is the orientation fixed prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k$, $1\le k\le4$,

i.e.

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}
0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$ .

Hence every $F_{3}$ gamete on the chosen strand starts with $0$ and ends
with $1$,

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,

and $x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}$ can be chosen independently.  For $a<k<b$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$

and for $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$ the product is the monotone $F_{1}$ word.
Thus on the fixed $0\to1$ phase

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$

is the $F_{3}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand.  For $n=5$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,

viz.

$01111,00111,00011,00001$  the four $F_{1}$ monotone gametes,
$01011,01001,01101,00101$  the four first genuine two-meiosis
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ mosaics.

The three interior SNPs $2,3,4$ are free in $F_{3}$ and no $1\ldots0$
word can ever be seen on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand because of
the stated strand asymmetry.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ $+$ strand haplotypes can be paired at
random.  Ordered maternal/paternal pairs are $H^{2}=64$ and up to order

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$

distinct unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand,
the $8$ haplotypes above being the distinct haploid chromosomes that can
be present in $F_{3}$.

Remark.  With the usual textbook book-keeping the formal telomeric
cuts $k=0,5$ are kept, $H_{1}^{+*}=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}$,
$|H_{1}^{+*}|=6$.  Two successive orientation-fixed prefix–suffix
replacements then give the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$
descent

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand
haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes, the $20=\binom{6}{3}$ words with $0\le a<k<b\le5$
being the conventional inclusive count.  Discarding the $k=0,5$ formal
ends this reduces to the strict obligatory interior crossover core
$2^{\,n-2}=8$ haplotypes, $36$ unordered diploid genotypes, quoted
above. ∎

9.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand we can put

$P_{0}=0^{5}\equiv00000$, $\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}\equiv11111$

and with the strand asymmetry the one break meiosis is the
orientation fixed prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}(i),\;i\le k,\;
{\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{b}(i),\;i>k ,
\qquad 1\le k\le4  $
on the $+$ strand.  Up to the formal $k=0,5$ ends

$h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad0\le t\le5,$

is the $0\to1$ monotone threshold.  With an obligatory internal
break $1\le k\le4$ the $P_{0}/P_{1}\to F_{1}$ gamete pool on the chosen
strand is

${\cal S}_{1}^{+}=\{0^{a}1^{5-a}:1\le a\le4\}
   =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$ , $|{\cal S}_{1}^{+}|=4$,

the two formal founders $0^{5},1^{5}$ being $k=0,5$ limits.  An $F_{2}$
is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
gamete is

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=
0^{\min(a,k)}1^{\,k-\min(a,k)}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4,
$

so that $z_{1}=0$, $z_{5}=1$ for every product.  In particular

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad
a<k<b,$

and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Writing
$z=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ we obtain

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{0xxx1\}$

on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation.  Hence

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$

distinct $+$–strand chromosomes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete
and therefore by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,

$\;01111,00111,00011,00001,\;01011,01001,01101,00101\;$,

the four monotone $F_{1}$ words $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the
four first genuine two–meiosis $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.  No $1\ldots0$ word can ever be seen on
the chosen strand; the three interior SNPs are free in $F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $H=8$ $+$–strand haplotypes can be paired at
random.  Up to maternal/paternal exchange there are

$N_{g}^{\rm unord}=\binom{H+1}{2}=H(H+1)/2=8\cdot9/2=36$

unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the fixed strand, $H^{2}=64$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs.  This is the obligatory-internal
$k=1\ldots4$ realisation of the orientation-fixed two-step set.

Remark.  Keeping the formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ as book-keeping
recombinants the $F_{1}$ pool is enlarged to the six monotone
thresholds $0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, and the two-step
orientation-fixed set is

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

i.e. the $0\to1$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  Then

$|H_{2}^{+*}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

$+$–strand haplotypes, $6$ monotone and $20=\binom63$ one-descent
mosaics, are attainable in the inclusive $k=0,5$ convention,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed strand, of which the $2^{\,n-2}=8$
$0xxx1$ words above are the strict obligatory-internal-crossover
core. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand we can write the two inbred founders as $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$. With the stated strand asymmetry a meiosis can be seen on the + strand only in the $0\to1$ orientation, i.e. as an orientation-fixed prefix–suffix

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})[i]=h_{a}[i]\,i\le k,\;h_{b}[i]\,i>k$.

With conventional book-keeping $h_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$, $0\le t\le5$, is the $F_{1}$ monotone pool on the + strand, $|H_{1}|=n+1=6$, the $k=0,5$ limits being the formal no-crossover ends.

An $F_{2}$ is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a},h_{b}\in H_{1}$ and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is again an orientation-fixed prefix–suffix.  With $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$

${\rm rec}_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $m=\min(a,k)$.

Up to the formal ends this is

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

a + strand word with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The triple $(a,k,b)$ is uniquely recovered from the word: $a$ is the length of the initial $0$ run, $k$ the end of the first $1$ run and $b$ the end of the second $0$ run, so distinct triples give distinct + strand haplotypes.

The six monotone thresholds $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $a\ge k$ or $k\ge b$ cases.  The genuinely new $F_{3}$ mosaics are $0\le a<k<b\le5$.  Their number is

$\#\{0\le a<k<b\le5\}=\binom{n+1}{3}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

$N_{1}(k)=k(5-k)$ per break, $\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=20$.

Hence on the fixed $0\to1$ orientation

$|H_{+}|=(n+1)+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different + strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ gamete and therefore by an $F_{3}$ chromosome: the six monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ $F_{1}$ thresholds and the twenty one-descent words $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.

In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand.

The $2^{\,n-2}=8$ words $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ is the physically strict obligatory-internal-crossover core obtained by discarding the formal telomeric $k=0,5$ ends, i.e. the $k=1\ldots4$, $a,b=1\ldots4$ realisation of the same construction.

The $2\sum_{i=0}^{3}\binom{4}{i}=30=2^{5}-2$ set is the maximal combinatorial set obtained only if the reciprocal $1\to0$ phase is counted as a distinct first-meiosis product on the same strand.  With sufficient strand asymmetry recombination is realised in only one orientation on the arbitrarily chosen + strand, so the $1\to0$ mirror half of the 30 set is not realisable on that strand.  $30$ is therefore a phase double count of the $26$ $0\to1$ words above. ∎

and up to the $k=0,5$ book-keeping ends

$h_{a,k,b}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

i.e. a + strand word with an initial $0$-run of length $a$, a first

distinct + strand haplotypes.  The six monotone thresholds are the
$a\ge k$ or $k\ge b$ cases.  The genuinely new $F_{3}$ mosaics are

$0\le a<k<b\le5$,

$N_{1}= \#\{0\le a<k<b\le5\}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.  In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes
on the chosen strand.

Discarding the formal telomeric $k=0,5$ limits the physically strict
obligatory-interior-crossover core is
$1\le a,k,b\le4$, $a<k<b$, and

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}=\{0xxx1\}$,
